answers.exactQuestionText:
What type of RFP/document is this?
(system implementation / framework agreeme...
answers.answerText: Open Framework Agreement for consulting engagements covering Business Process Reengineering (BPR), government services improvement, organizational transformation and digital transformation consulting. It is an umbrella procurement framework rather than one fixed implementation project.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the document/RFP title?
answers.answerText: OPEN FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT FOR REEGENIRING PROJECTS (as written on the cover; the document concerns Business Process Reengineering / Reengineering Projects).

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the beneficiary entity / ministry?
answers.answerText: Contracting/framework owner: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE), Jordan. Beneficiaries of individual assignments are MoDEE and the relevant governmental entities covered by each project-specific Scope of Work (SOW).

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the RFP or tender number (if any)?
What is the deadline?
answers.answerText: The cover states 1 July 2026. However, the Response Submission section and related administrative clauses still contain blank deadline placeholders, so the final JONEPS/official submission date should be confirmed before issue.

answers.exactQuestionText: Language is English only for now (do not ask for Arabic/bilingual in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: The RFP is primarily in English. The Joint Venture Agreement is bilingual Arabic/English and states that Arabic is authentic in case of interpretation differences. No universal language requirement for all framework deliverables is explicitly stated in the main document.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which approved template or reference RFP should be followed?
answers.answerText: Key governing references include Annex 5.1 MoDEE Business Process Reengineering Standards, Confidentiality Undertaking, Joint Venture Agreement, Sample Framework Agreement, Supplier Security Assessment Questionnaire, bidder-information and anti-corruption forms, plus attached MoDEE security, customer-journey, performance, SDLC, portal-design and API standards referenced in the annex list.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: MoDEE leads public-sector digital transformation and works with government entities on service improvement, procedure simplification, customer experience and institutional performance. Instead of procuring one fixed BPR project, MoDEE is establishing a five-year pool of qualified consulting firms that can be called for different government transformation assignments as needs arise.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: No single entity-specific pain-point baseline is defined at framework level. The framework is designed to address project-specific bottlenecks, redundancies, manual interventions, inefficiencies, customer-journey issues, governance gaps, regulatory constraints and improvement opportunities discovered during each assignment.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: MoDEE needs a reusable procurement mechanism that can rapidly engage qualified consultants for recurring BPR, government-service improvement and organizational/digital transformation projects over five years, while maintaining consistent standards, methodologies, governance and quality controls.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Enable recurring government modernization assignments that discover and validate current-state processes, redesign future-state processes, improve efficiency/service quality/customer experience, identify automation and digital-enablement opportunities, define governance/KPI/SLA requirements, produce BRDs where needed, and prepare downstream digital-transformation RFP packages when required.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: No previous contract or prior framework is identified. Individual projects must align with existing MoDEE standards, ARIS/BPMN modeling conventions, government digital-transformation standards, security controls, customer-journey standards and other attached policies/annexes.

answers.exactQuestionText:
Is this a one-time project, framework agreement, system implementation,
consu...
answers.answerText: A five-year Open Framework Agreement for consulting services. It combines initial technical qualification with repeated project-specific competitions/SOWs among qualified framework contractors.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there phases? If yes, list them.
answers.answerText: Yes. Phase 1 is Technical Qualifications Evaluation with no financial proposal and no bid bond. Qualified bidders then enter Phase 2 and sign the five-year framework. During Phase 2, MoDEE issues project-specific SOWs, determines project-specific technical/financial evaluation criteria, requests proposals/pricing from qualified bidders and awards assignments based on project needs, performance and resource availability.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the expected duration?
answers.answerText: Framework duration: five years. The duration, milestones and schedule of each individual project are defined separately in its SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is the beneficiary / system owner?
answers.answerText: MoDEE is the framework owner and contracting/governance authority. Each assignment may have a different governmental entity as business beneficiary, with business owners and relevant internal/external stakeholders participating in discovery, validation and future-state design.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who are internal users? External users?
answers.answerText: There is no fixed application-user population at framework level. Relevant users/stakeholders vary by SOW and may include government employees/process owners, service-delivery teams, external customers/citizens and other parties involved in the targeted service/customer journey.

answers.exactQuestionText: What roles are required?
answers.answerText: Minimum framework resource profiles include: one Project Manager (5+ years, PMP or PRINCE2), one Senior BPR Consultant (7+ years and at least five similar completed projects, ARIS/BPMN capability), one Junior BPR Consultant (3+ years and at least one similar completed project, ARIS/BPMN capability), and one Business Analyst/Process Analyst (5+ years). MoDEE may request additional or replacement resources per SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?
answers.answerText: There is no software UAT at framework level. Project deliverables are validated through quality-assurance and stakeholder review sessions with MoDEE and relevant business representatives. Project-specific acceptance requirements and approval steps are defined in each SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who owns the system after go-live?
answers.answerText: Not applicable as a software go-live ownership question. Contract materials, reports, documents, software and other project material created under the framework vest in or become property of MoDEE subject to the stated IP/license provisions.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is in scope?
answers.answerText: Framework scope covers BPR, government-service improvement, organizational transformation and digital-transformation consulting. Annex 5.1 defines four reusable components: (1) Process Discovery & Current State Assessment; (2) Business Process Reengineering & Future State Design; (3) Digital Transformation Enablement, including BRD creation; and (4) Digital Transformation RFP preparation, including current-system assessment, detailed functional/non-functional/technical/integration/security requirements, SOW and evaluation criteria.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is out of scope?
answers.answerText: There is no single detailed out-of-scope list because this is an umbrella framework. The actual scope, special requirements, activities, deliverables and exclusions of each assignment are determined in its SOW. Software implementation itself is not automatically included merely because a BPR project identifies digital-enablement needs; a separate downstream Digital Transformation RFP may be an output.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are bidder responsibilities?
answers.answerText: Framework contractors must provide and maintain all required resources at no additional cost, comply with MoDEE standards and methodologies, perform the project-specific consulting scope, provide timely deliverables/milestones, use qualified ARIS/BPMN resources where required, support validation/quality review, and comply with contractual, confidentiality, security and reporting obligations. Exact responsibilities are refined per SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are MODEE / entity responsibilities?
answers.answerText: MoDEE qualifies contractors, signs the framework, prepares each SOW and its estimated time frame, defines project-specific evaluation criteria and proposal requirements, may request additional references/resources, approves/replaces resources, coordinates project/business stakeholders, reviews deliverables and controls the applicable standards/templates. Government entities provide project-specific business participation and validation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Assumptions, dependencies, constraints?
answers.answerText: Key framework constraints/dependencies include five-year duration; recurring re-opening to new applicants; project-specific SOWs and evaluation rules; variable resource needs; MoDEE resource approval/replacement rights; compliance with MoDEE BPR/digital/security standards; ARIS/BPMN modeling capability; availability/performance of firms across multiple assignments; and project-specific urgency, confidentiality or specialized expertise.

answers.exactQuestionText: Main modules / services?
answers.answerText: Reusable service components are: Current-State/Process Discovery; Future-State BPR; Digital Transformation Enablement; and preparation of Digital Transformation RFP/procurement packages. Depending on the SOW, outputs may also include BRDs, gap analysis, RACI, KPI/SLA recommendations, policy/regulatory recommendations, forms/templates and current-system assessments.

answers.exactQuestionText: Key workflows / approvals?
answers.answerText: Typical framework workflow: project need identified → MoDEE prepares SOW and evaluation criteria → qualified framework firms are invited → proposals/pricing evaluated → assignment awarded → workshops/interviews/current-state assessment → As-Is modeling/gap analysis → To-Be redesign → digital-readiness/integration analysis → BRD and/or downstream digital-transformation RFP where required → validation/approval → milestone/deliverable completion.

answers.exactQuestionText: Reports / dashboards / notifications needed?
answers.answerText: Expected outputs include current-state architecture and As-Is models, gap analysis, stakeholder matrices, To-Be models, RACI, process-improvement recommendations, KPI/SLA recommendations, policies/regulatory amendment report, forms/templates catalogue, BRD, current-systems assessment, Digital Transformation RFP and technical/financial evaluation criteria. Generic dashboard/notification requirements are not stated.

answers.exactQuestionText: Document management / case / ticketing needs?
answers.answerText: No enterprise document/case/ticketing system is being procured at framework level. Process models are documented in ARIS and supporting deliverables/documents follow MoDEE standards. A later project-specific digital implementation may define case/document-management needs through its BRD/RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: Any AI or advanced features required/optional?
answers.answerText: No AI capability is required at framework level. If an individual SOW or downstream Digital Transformation RFP involves AI, those requirements would need to be defined project-specifically.

answers.exactQuestionText: Hosting / infrastructure model?
answers.answerText: No hosting/infrastructure model applies to the generic consulting framework. Digital landscape, system constraints and implementation environment are assessed only when required by a project-specific Digital Transformation Enablement/RFP assignment.

answers.exactQuestionText: Integrations / APIs?
answers.answerText: No fixed API/integration list exists at framework level. Future-state work must assess digital readiness, integration requirements and interdependencies, and downstream Digital Transformation RFPs must define detailed integration requirements for the specific project.

answers.exactQuestionText: Security / data residency requirements?
answers.answerText: Framework contractors must comply with MoDEE secrecy/security requirements, confidentiality undertakings, Supplier Security Assessment Questionnaire and attached security/SDLC/API policies where applicable. Specific application security/data-residency requirements depend on the individual SOW or downstream implementation RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: Performance / availability / backup / DR?
answers.answerText: No universal system availability, backup or DR targets exist at framework level. The BPR standards require definition/recommendation of process KPIs and SLAs, while project-specific digital RFPs may define non-functional/performance requirements separately.

answers.exactQuestionText: Data migration needs?
answers.answerText: No generic data-migration requirement applies. The closest framework-level transition output is gap analysis and implementation/execution planning between As-Is and To-Be, while any actual data migration would be defined in the downstream implementation SOW/RFP if relevant.

answers.exactQuestionText: Accessibility requirements? (English drafting only in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: No explicit universal accessibility requirement is stated in the main BPR scope. However, the annex list references Customer Journey Experience Standards and e-services portal design standards/guidelines, which may apply to project-specific digital-service work. Exact accessibility requirements should therefore be confirmed per SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: What documents/reports/designs/tests/training materials are required?
answers.answerText: Framework-standard deliverables include: Current State Process Architecture (VACD); detailed As-Is BPMN models in ARIS; As-Is stakeholder matrix; Gap Analysis Report; To-Be ARIS models; RACI Matrix; Process Improvement Recommendations; SLA/KPI Recommendations; Policies/Regulations/Legislative Amendment Report; To-Be Forms and Templates Catalogue; To-Be stakeholder matrix; BRD; current-systems assessment; Digital Transformation RFP; and technical/financial evaluation criteria. Each SOW may add or remove deliverables.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required formats?
answers.answerText: As-Is/To-Be process models are explicitly documented on the ARIS platform using MoDEE filter/BPMN standards. Other document formats are not universally specified at framework level; project-specific formats/templates are governed by MoDEE standards and the SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves each deliverable?
answers.answerText: MoDEE and relevant government/business stakeholders validate and approve deliverables through QA/review sessions. Exact deliverable acceptance owners, review periods and sign-off procedures are to be defined in the project-specific SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Stages, timeline, milestones?
answers.answerText: There is no universal implementation timeline for assignments. Each SOW contains clearly defined deliverables, milestones, implementation schedule and estimated completion time. The overarching framework lasts five years.

answers.exactQuestionText: Testing / UAT rounds?
answers.answerText: Traditional software testing/UAT is not a generic framework requirement. BPR deliverables undergo quality assurance, stakeholder validation and review. If an assignment produces a downstream digital implementation RFP, that RFP should define testing/UAT requirements appropriate to that implementation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Acceptance criteria and go-live conditions?
answers.answerText: Acceptance is project/deliverable based. Each SOW defines milestones and deliverables, while MoDEE/business stakeholders validate the consulting outputs. Framework terms allow contractual action for unjustified delay or failure to meet agreed deliverables/milestones.

answers.exactQuestionText: Rollback plan needed?
answers.answerText: No generic rollback plan is required for BPR consulting. Transition or implementation planning for To-Be processes may be included in project-specific scope, and downstream digital implementation RFPs can define rollback/cutover requirements if needed.

answers.exactQuestionText: Support period and hours?
answers.answerText: No generic post-go-live support period or support hours are defined because the framework is for consulting assignments. Any support/operations requirement would be determined in the specific SOW or downstream implementation RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: Severity levels / response / resolution times?
answers.answerText: No generic incident severity, response or resolution SLA matrix applies to framework consulting services. Process KPI/SLA recommendations may be a deliverable, but they are business-process recommendations rather than support commitments of the consultant.

answers.exactQuestionText: Resident engineer / ticketing / reports?
answers.answerText: No resident engineer/helpdesk/ticketing model is defined. Project teams and single points of contact are required as appropriate, and MoDEE may request additional/replacement resources. Project-specific reporting/support expectations are set in the SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Penalties?
answers.answerText: The framework allows contractual measures for unjustified delays/failure to meet agreed deliverables and milestones, including suspension or termination. The general legal terms also reference delay penalties in the Sample Framework Agreement, but exact project penalties are determined contractually/per assignment.

answers.exactQuestionText: Technical vs financial weights?
answers.answerText: Phase 1 has no financial proposal and is a technical qualification gate. Qualified firms proceed to Phase 2. For each Phase-2 SOW, MoDEE independently determines the technical and financial evaluation criteria and proposal requirements, so there is no single framework-wide technical/financial weighting.

answers.exactQuestionText: Minimum score / PoC scoring / disqualification rules?
answers.answerText: There is no numeric technical score stated for Phase 1 in the main RFP. Failure to provide the required reference project/accomplishment letter, commitment to required CVs/qualifications, or compliance with MoDEE standards/components leads to disqualification. Additional project-specific qualification requirements may be imposed for each SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Pricing model and cost breakdown requirements?
answers.answerText: No prices are submitted in Phase 1. During Phase 2 each assignment is priced from qualified bidders. General financial terms specify JOD, all-inclusive fixed lump-sum pricing, inclusive of expenses/fees/taxes/sales tax, with a clear breakdown of consulting time and other expenses; payments follow accepted project scope, deliverables and milestones.

answers.exactQuestionText: Optional priced items? Taxes?
answers.answerText: There is no universal optional-price list at framework level. Scope and pricing are SOW-specific. Performance-bond value/timing are also decided separately for each assignment. Any optional or separately priced project element should therefore be identified in the individual SOW rather than the framework qualification.

answers.exactQuestionText: Applicable laws / confidentiality / IP?
answers.answerText: Applicable terms include the laws/regulations of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, Government Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and its Instructions, the binding Sample Framework Agreement, confidentiality/NDA obligations, secrecy/security, conflict-of-interest rules, anti-corruption/fraud provisions, IP/document-property rules, liability/indemnity and the World Bank Anti-Corruption Guidelines/Sanctions Framework acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Joint venture / subcontracting rules?
answers.answerText: Joint ventures and subcontracting are permitted subject to stated conditions. JV members are jointly and severally liable, must appoint a leader and sign the provided agreement; the winning JV agreement is notarized. Subcontractors require MoDEE approval and the prime contractor remains liable for their work.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required forms, compliance sheets, questionnaires, annexes?
answers.answerText: The RFP references numerous mandatory/controlling annexes, including MoDEE BPR Standards/Compliance, Confidentiality Undertaking, Joint Venture Agreement, Sample Framework Agreement, Supplier Security Assessment Questionnaire, bidder-information form, World Bank anti-corruption letter, and attached security/customer-journey/performance/SDLC/design/API standards. The exact annex numbering is inconsistent across the document.

answers.exactQuestionText: What must not be missed in this RFP?
answers.answerText: Do not miss: five-year open framework; two-phase qualification/implementation model; recurring admission of new firms every three months; no financial proposal or bid bond in Phase 1; per-SOW scope/evaluation/pricing/milestones; MoDEE rights to request additional/replacement resources and to balance/limit awards based on performance/resource availability; minimum BPR resource profiles; mandatory MoDEE standards/ARIS-BPMN compliance; BPR As-Is/To-Be + digital-enablement + downstream Digital Transformation RFP capability; security/confidentiality/legal requirements; and project-specific performance bonds.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mistakes happened in previous similar RFPs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the source does not document lessons or mistakes from previous similar framework procurements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which parts usually cause vendor questions or scope disputes?
answers.answerText: Likely clarification/dispute areas include framework re-opening/admission mechanics, how project invitations/allocations are balanced, when MoDEE may invite only selected qualified firms, project-specific evaluation criteria, resource concurrency/availability, performance-bond values, exact SOW acceptance/payment rules, applicable annex versions, and the distinction between BPR consulting versus downstream digital implementation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which requirements are mandatory, optional, excluded, or pending approval?
answers.answerText: Phase-1 mandatory: required BPR/transformation reference and accomplishment letter, commitment to provide required CVs/certifications, and compliance with MoDEE standards/components. No Phase-1 financial proposal or bid bond is required. Phase-2 scope, resources, deliverables, evaluation, pricing, milestones, bonds and any optional/excluded items are determined per SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: What should be priced separately as optional?
answers.answerText: Nothing is universally priced as an optional framework item in Phase 1. Each project SOW determines what must be priced and whether any optional/separate items exist. Framework financial terms otherwise expect all-inclusive fixed lump-sum project pricing.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is still unknown and should be [To be confirmed]?
answers.answerText: Key TBCs include: final authoritative submission/clarification dates because the body contains placeholders; future project/SOW list and quantities; each project's detailed scope, beneficiary, schedule, deliverables, evaluation criteria and payment plan; performance-bond value/timing; project-specific resource quantities; exact acceptance periods; which qualified firms will be invited to each selective SOW; and final applicable annex/version numbering.

answers.exactQuestionText: Should Rami generate a risk/ambiguity list before final drafting?
answers.answerText: Yes, as an internal Rami quality-control step. This RFP contains several structural/copy-paste inconsistencies and deliberately deferred SOW-level information; Rami should distinguish 'legitimately deferred to SOW' from 'missing/contradictory in the framework document' before drafting.

answers.exactQuestionText: What standards, policies, or annexes must be referenced?
answers.answerText: References include MoDEE BPR Standards, ARIS/BPMN modeling conventions, MoDEE digital-transformation/governance/customer-journey/security standards, Supplier Security Assessment Questionnaire, Confidentiality Undertaking, Sample Framework Agreement, Government Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and Instructions, World Bank Anti-Corruption Guidelines/Sanctions Framework, and the attached SDLC/API/e-service design/performance standards as applicable.

answers.exactQuestionText: For an open framework, when and how may new suppliers join after the initial award?
answers.answerText: New companies may request participation during the five-year term. The framework re-opens every three months for one week after the first framework agreements are signed, with periods announced by MoDEE.

answers.exactQuestionText: How are individual assignments/SOWs initiated and what minimum information must each SOW contain?
answers.answerText: MoDEE prepares each SOW, including special requirements/activities/deliverables and estimated completion time; project deliverables, milestones and implementation schedule must be clearly defined.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is invited to each SOW: all qualified suppliers or a selected subset, and under what exceptions?
answers.answerText: Generally SOW pricing is requested from qualified bidders, but MoDEE may invite selected qualified contractors based on project-specific requirements, urgency, confidentiality, continuity, specialized expertise, resource availability or past performance.

answers.exactQuestionText: How are assignments distributed across qualified framework suppliers and how are equal-opportunity/resource-capacity considerations handled?
answers.answerText: MoDEE determines the number of projects awarded to each company based on available projects, number of qualified companies, running projects, company performance and resource availability, with the stated aim of equal opportunity.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which qualification/evaluation criteria remain fixed at framework level and which may be redefined per SOW?
answers.answerText: Framework entry requires the stated BPR reference/accomplishment/CV commitment/standards compliance. MoDEE may define new technical and financial evaluation criteria, additional references and additional resources for each SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: What commercial/security instruments are framework-level versus assignment-level?
answers.answerText: No Phase-1 bid bond or financial proposal. Assignment pricing is Phase 2; the performance-bond value and timing are determined separately for each assignment.

answers.exactQuestionText: What happens when a framework contractor is underperforming, overcommitted, or lacks a suitable resource?
answers.answerText: MoDEE may request resource replacement, consider company performance/resource availability when allocating work, apply contractual measures for delay/failure, and can suspend/terminate where applicable.

answers.exactQuestionText: What proposal validity, withdrawal, alternative-proposal and non-responsiveness rules apply to framework qualification?
answers.answerText: Proposal validity is 90 days; alternative proposals/reservations are prohibited; technical proposals may not include price; withdrawals/modifications are allowed before deadline under the stated rules; non-compliance can result in rejection/disqualification.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mandatory framework annexes/forms/security declarations must be completed even if a specific project SOW has not yet been issued?
answers.answerText: BPR standards/compliance, confidentiality undertaking, JV agreement where applicable, supplier security assessment, bidder information and anti-corruption acceptance are among the required framework artefacts.

answers.exactQuestionText: What information is intentionally deferred to each future SOW and must not be invented in the framework RFP?
answers.answerText: Beneficiary/project title, exact process inventory, scope/exclusions, deliverables, milestones, duration, evaluation criteria, resource quantities, price/payment, performance bond, acceptance rules and any project-specific technical requirements are deferred to the SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: For BPR/transformation assignments, what process/service inventory and customer channels are in scope?
answers.answerText: Defined per SOW. The framework requires discovery of processes, service-delivery workflows, customer journeys, touchpoints/channels and related application requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: What current-state discovery methods and As-Is modeling outputs are mandatory?
answers.answerText: Workshops/interviews/stakeholder meetings; analysis of procedures/workflows; identification of gaps/bottlenecks/redundancy/manual work; laws/governance/forms review; customer-journey assessment; VACD current-state architecture; detailed BPMN As-Is models in ARIS; stakeholder matrix; gap report.

answers.exactQuestionText: What future-state redesign outputs must be defined beyond process diagrams?
answers.answerText: To-Be ARIS models, RACI, process-improvement recommendations, SLA/KPI recommendations, policy/regulatory amendment report, To-Be forms/templates catalogue and To-Be stakeholder matrix.

answers.exactQuestionText: What laws, regulations, policies, forms, templates and business rules must be reviewed or changed to enable the To-Be state?
answers.answerText: The framework requires review of applicable laws/policies/governance/forms during As-Is and identification of legislative/regulatory/procedural amendments, business rules, decision points and new forms/templates for To-Be.

answers.exactQuestionText: What digital-readiness, automation, integration and system-dependency analysis is required for the To-Be processes?
answers.answerText: Consultants assess digital readiness, integration requirements/interdependencies and current digital landscape, then identify digitization, automation, system-integration and digital-service opportunities.

answers.exactQuestionText: When must a BRD be produced, and what business/functional/non-functional requirements must it capture?
answers.answerText: Digital Transformation Enablement may require a BRD defining business, functional and non-functional requirements plus digital-enablement needs for implementation of the approved future-state processes.

answers.exactQuestionText: When is the consultant expected to produce a downstream Digital Transformation RFP rather than implement the technology directly?
answers.answerText: Where the project requires digital implementation, the framework may require current-system assessment, detailed functional/non-functional/technical/integration/security requirements, SOW and a full Digital Transformation RFP/procurement package with evaluation criteria.

answers.exactQuestionText: What process KPIs, SLAs, governance model and RACI must be established for the redesigned operating model?
answers.answerText: The framework requires governance models/RACI and KPI/SLA/governance requirements, with SLA/KPI recommendations as a formal deliverable.

answers.exactQuestionText: What modeling platform, notation, filters and MoDEE conventions are mandatory?
answers.answerText: As-Is and To-Be models must use ARIS/BPMN and MoDEE-approved modeling standards/filters; bidders must provide capable resources if their proposed BPR team lacks ARIS capability.

answers.exactQuestionText: What quality-assurance, stakeholder-validation and acceptance approach is required for BPR outputs?
answers.answerText: Current-state findings and future-state deliverables must be validated through QA and stakeholder review sessions with MoDEE and relevant business stakeholders; detailed project acceptance rules are then set in the SOW.

answers.exactQuestionText: Does the engagement stop at BPR recommendations, or must it also prepare implementation-ready procurement artefacts?
answers.answerText: It may extend beyond BPR to implementation-ready artefacts: BRD, current-system assessment, detailed technical/integration/security requirements, SOW, Digital Transformation RFP and technical/financial evaluation criteria.

What type of RFP/document is this?
(system implementation / framework agreeme...
answers.answerText: Pre-Qualification (PQ) document for a future system implementation. The procurement aims to shortlist technically and financially capable firms for the design, development, deployment, and maintenance of the SANAD AI national AI chatbot platform. This is not yet the final implementation RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the document/RFP title?
answers.answerText: Agentic Chatbot (SANAD AI) — Pre-Qualification.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the beneficiary entity / ministry?
answers.answerText: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE), Jordan. The platform is intended to serve Jordanian citizens accessing e-government services.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the RFP or tender number (if any)?
What is the deadline?
Language is English only for now (do not ask for Arabic/bilingual in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: The PQ document is primarily in English. The proposed SANAD AI solution itself must be bilingual, Arabic and English, with Arabic-first behavior and support for Jordanian Arabic dialects.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which approved template or reference RFP should be followed?
answers.answerText: The governing reference for this stage is the SANAD AI Pre-Qualification document, including its Qualification Matrix, Bidder/Joint Venture Expertise Form, Joint Venture Agreement form, and Financial Solvency form. The final Stage 2 tender documents are not included here and will be issued only to pre-qualified bidders.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: MoDEE intends to create SANAD AI as a unified national conversational interface between Jordanian citizens and government services. The future platform will span multiple channels and connect to existing SANAD portals, government APIs, the NSR database, authentication/payment/document services, and existing CRM/call-center systems.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: The PQ does not provide a detailed current-state pain-point study. The implied needs are fragmented citizen access across government services/channels, the need for real-time contextual assistance, bilingual/Jordanian-Arabic support, trusted knowledge retrieval, secure integration with government systems, scalable AI infrastructure, and consistent omnichannel service delivery.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: The project is intended to advance national digital government by giving citizens a single intelligent conversational entry point to information, guided interactions and transactional services. The PQ is being conducted now to shortlist firms capable of delivering the complex AI, integration, infrastructure and security requirements before the final tender stage.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Provide a national Arabic-first, bilingual, omnichannel AI assistant that delivers accurate/context-aware answers; supports information, interaction and transactional government services; integrates with SANAD/government APIs and knowledge sources; reduces hallucinations through RAG/controlled knowledge; supports Jordanian dialects; enables secure transactions; and provides scalable, accessible, continuously improving citizen service.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: Yes. The future solution must integrate with the existing SANAD ecosystem, SANAD portals/mobile app, government APIs, NSR database, authentication/payment/document services, and existing CRM/call-center systems. Exact legacy architecture and current system details are not provided in this PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there phases? If yes, list them.
answers.answerText: Yes. Stage 1: submit a no-price technical pre-qualification proposal, feature/function list, qualifications, experience, staffing and financial-solvency evidence; the committee may negotiate and shortlist. Stage 2: qualified bidders submit full technical and financial proposals and a pilot/PoC for the AI engine under the final tender documents.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the expected duration?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — this PQ does not state the implementation or maintenance duration for the future SANAD AI contract.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is the beneficiary / system owner?
answers.answerText: MoDEE is the contracting authority and future platform owner/operator. Jordanian citizens are the primary service beneficiaries; multiple government entities and SANAD ecosystem services are stakeholders/integration partners.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who are internal users? External users?
answers.answerText: External users: Jordanian citizens using SANAD AI across web, SANAD mobile, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and future voice channels. Internal/operational users likely include MoDEE technical teams, administrators, analysts, live agents/call-center users and integration teams; exact user counts and operational personas are not stated in the PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: What roles are required?
answers.answerText: Minimum bidder team includes: 1 Project Manager; 2 AI/NLP Solution Architects; 2 Machine Learning/Data Engineers; 3 Software/System Engineers; 1 Technical Consultant/Integration Specialist; 1 AI Linguist/Arabic Language Specialist; 1 Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Specialist; 2 DBAs; 2 Business Analyst/UX Specialists; 1 QA Engineer; and 1 Training & Change Management Specialist, with specified experience thresholds.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?
answers.answerText: The PQ itself is evaluated by the procurement committee. For Stage 2, qualified bidders must submit a pilot/PoC for the AI engine. Detailed UAT, business approval, acceptance governance and go-live approval roles for the implementation are [To be confirmed] in the final tender.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who owns the system after go-live?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — system ownership after go-live is not explicitly stated in this PQ, although MoDEE is clearly the contracting authority and intended operator of the national platform.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is in scope?
answers.answerText: High-level future scope includes: architecture/data-flow design; integration with SANAD and government APIs; hybrid infrastructure; AI model customization for Arabic/Jordanian dialects and English; development/testing/deployment across web, SANAD mobile, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and future voice; RAG/NLU/LLM capabilities; information, guided-interaction and transactional services; live-agent handover; sentiment/feedback analytics; training/knowledge transfer; maintenance/continuous improvement; cybersecurity, privacy and accessibility compliance; and bidder-managed GPU infrastructure for open-data AI training/optimization.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is out of scope?
answers.answerText: The PQ does not provide a formal out-of-scope list. Voice interaction is explicitly optional. API management scope, detailed channel limits, model ownership/licensing boundaries, exact data domains and which government services will be transaction-enabled are not defined and should remain [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: What are bidder responsibilities?
answers.answerText: At PQ level, bidders must demonstrate capability to design/develop/deploy/maintain the platform, integrate APIs and government services, provide/manage AI/GPU infrastructure, customize AI/NLP/LLM/RAG capabilities, satisfy cybersecurity/data-protection requirements, support Arabic/Jordanian dialects, provide training/knowledge transfer/support, and submit valid qualification evidence. Exact contractual implementation responsibilities are deferred to Stage 2.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are MODEE / entity responsibilities?
answers.answerText: MoDEE will govern the procurement, provide/operate the on-premises part of the hybrid environment, provide access to SANAD/government systems and APIs as applicable, and evaluate/shortlist bidders. Detailed responsibilities for data preparation, API readiness, content ownership, integration testing, live-agent operations and production governance are [To be confirmed] in Stage 2.

answers.exactQuestionText: Assumptions, dependencies, constraints?
answers.answerText: Key constraints/dependencies include two-stage procurement; hybrid hosting; all data stored within Jordan; separation of non-open data on MoDEE on-premises from bidder-provided GPU infrastructure for open-data AI training/optimization; integration with existing SANAD/government APIs; Arabic/Jordanian dialect quality; strict knowledge/RAG to reduce hallucinations; cybersecurity/privacy compliance; and qualification evidence/certification requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Main modules / services?
answers.answerText: Primary service groups: (1) Information Services — government information, FAQs, requirements and retrieval from SANAD/NSR; (2) Interaction Services — guided journeys, eligibility checks, form assistance, appointment scheduling, proactive notifications; (3) Transactional Services — end-to-end execution of selected e-government services. Platform capabilities also include omnichannel delivery, RAG/knowledge integration, live-agent handover, sentiment/feedback and analytics.

answers.exactQuestionText: Key workflows / approvals?
answers.answerText: High-level workflows include citizen query → intent/context understanding → knowledge/API retrieval → response/guidance; guided service journey → eligibility/form/appointment support; transactional flow → authentication/payment/document retrieval through SANAD APIs; escalation to live agent when required; and proactive notification/reminder flows. Exact approval/process rules for each government service are [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: Reports / dashboards / notifications needed?
answers.answerText: Required analytics/reporting include dashboards for conversation analytics, service usage and performance metrics, plus sentiment/feedback analysis and escalation triggers. Detailed KPI definitions, operational dashboards, audit reporting and executive reporting are [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: Document management / case / ticketing needs?
answers.answerText: No separate document/case-management platform is explicitly required. However, transactional services may retrieve documents, and live-agent handover must integrate with existing CRM/call-center platforms such as Genesys or Zendesk. Detailed ticket/case lifecycle requirements are [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: Any AI or advanced features required/optional?
answers.answerText: Yes. AI is central to the project: LLMs, RAG, NLP/NLU, contextual understanding, intent recognition, dialogue management, Jordanian Arabic adaptation, sentiment analysis, optional Arabic ASR/TTS/voice interaction, analytics, and continuous AI model optimization/improvement.

answers.exactQuestionText: Hosting / infrastructure model?
answers.answerText: Hybrid hosting: MoDEE on-premises plus bidder-provided GPU clusters. The on-premises component is specified for non-open data, while bidder-managed GPU infrastructure is required for AI model training and optimization for open data. Exact production inference placement and environment topology are not fully defined.

answers.exactQuestionText: Integrations / APIs?
answers.answerText: Integrations include existing SANAD and government APIs, SANAD portals/mobile, NSR database, authentication, payments and document retrieval, existing CRM/call-center systems, and multiple external communication channels. The qualification matrix also expects experience integrating with government APIs, e-service platforms and identity-management systems.

answers.exactQuestionText: Security / data residency requirements?
answers.answerText: All data must be stored within Jordan. The system must comply with MoDEE cybersecurity standards and local privacy/data-residency requirements, use AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit and zero-trust RBAC principles. Qualification also expects ISO 27001, NIST or equivalent security evidence.

answers.exactQuestionText: Performance / availability / backup / DR?
answers.answerText: The solution must be secure and scalable and support real-time conversational service, but this PQ does not specify numeric availability, latency, throughput, RTO/RPO, backup or disaster-recovery targets. These are [To be confirmed] for Stage 2.

answers.exactQuestionText: Data migration needs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no explicit legacy data-migration scope is stated. Knowledge ingestion, content preparation, vector/RAG indexing and model/data onboarding will likely be relevant to implementation, but detailed migration requirements are not defined in this PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: Accessibility requirements? (English drafting only in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: The solution must comply with WCAG 2.1 AA and provide an inclusive, accessible, user-centric experience. Optional voice interaction through Arabic ASR/TTS is also positioned as an accessibility/inclusivity capability.

answers.exactQuestionText: What documents/reports/designs/tests/training materials are required?
answers.answerText: This PQ does not define a complete implementation deliverables list. It does require qualification evidence including technical proposal, features/functions list, project references/completion certificates, architecture/API summaries, infrastructure specifications, security certificates/audits, team CVs, financial solvency form, joint-venture documentation where applicable, and completed evaluation forms. Stage 2 implementation deliverables remain [To be confirmed].

answers.answerText: Pre-qualification submission must be a technical proposal in a sealed envelope labeled 'Technical Offer – SANAD AI Project', with required forms accurately completed. Detailed implementation deliverable formats are not specified at this stage.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves each deliverable?
answers.answerText: At PQ stage, the procurement committee evaluates the submission and qualification evidence. Implementation-stage deliverable approval authorities are [To be confirmed] in the Stage 2 tender.

answers.exactQuestionText: Stages, timeline, milestones?
answers.answerText: Stage 1 and Stage 2 are defined, but no detailed implementation stages, timeline or milestones are provided. The only explicit date in this PQ is the 18/5/2026 submission deadline. Detailed project implementation period will be part of Stage 2.

answers.exactQuestionText: Testing / UAT rounds?
answers.answerText: A pilot/PoC for the AI engine is required from qualified bidders in Stage 2. Detailed testing rounds — functional, security, model evaluation, red-teaming, hallucination, UAT, load/performance, accessibility and integration testing — are not specified in this PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: Acceptance criteria and go-live conditions?
answers.answerText: Stage 1 qualification depends on meeting technical/financial eligibility and evidence requirements. Stage 2 includes an AI pilot/PoC, but final system acceptance/go-live criteria are [To be confirmed] in the final tender.

answers.exactQuestionText: Rollback plan needed?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no rollback/cutover requirement is stated in the PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: Support period and hours?
answers.answerText: Maintenance and continuous improvement are in the intended future scope, but the support period and support hours are not stated in this PQ.

answers.answerText: Training, documentation and ongoing technical support are required at high level, but no resident engineer, ticketing model, support staffing or service-reporting requirements are defined in this PQ.

answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no operational SLA penalties are specified in the PQ.

answers.answerText: This PQ does not provide a final technical-versus-financial award weighting because Stage 1 is a pre-qualification gate, not final commercial evaluation. answers.answerText: Qualification is threshold/disqualification based. Examples: at least one completed AI chatbot/conversational-platform project; evidence of Arabic-first NLP; at least one LLM+RAG project; government/public-sector integration experience; GPU hosting capability; staff CV collective marks of at least 36; security certification/evidence; unaltered financial solvency form; good-performance certificates; and preliminary JV agreement where applicable. Missing required evidence can cause disqualification.

answers.exactQuestionText: Pricing model and cost breakdown requirements?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no implementation pricing model or cost breakdown is requested at Stage 1 because bidders submit pre-qualification technical proposals without prices. Financial capability is assessed through a bank-issued financial solvency certificate/form.

answers.exactQuestionText: Optional priced items? Taxes?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no Stage 2 optional pricing or tax structure is stated in this PQ. Voice interaction is functionally optional, but its commercial treatment is not defined.

answers.answerText: Joint ventures are permitted with a maximum of two members between Jordanian and international firms. A preliminary JV Agreement signed by all parties is mandatory for qualification. Detailed subcontracting rules are not stated.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required forms, compliance sheets, questionnaires, annexes?
answers.answerText: Required forms/evidence include the Bidder/Joint Venture Expertise Form, Financial Solvency Form, completion/good-performance certificates, project references, staff CVs, infrastructure details, security certificates/audits, technical evaluation forms, and preliminary Joint Venture Agreement where applicable.

answers.exactQuestionText: What evidence creates pass/fail qualification, and which missing documents cause automatic disqualification?
answers.answerText: AI/chatbot references, Arabic NLP evidence, LLM+RAG experience, government integration evidence, GPU hosting details, staff marks ≥36, security certificates/audits, financial solvency form, good-performance certificates and JV agreement where applicable.

answers.answerText: An original certificate from an approved bank strictly following the prescribed Financial Solvency Form. Any modification to the form causes disqualification.

answers.answerText: JV is allowed with a maximum of two members between Jordanian and international firms. A preliminary JV Agreement signed by all parties is mandatory.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pilot, PoC, demo, or validation exercise will be required after qualification?
answers.answerText: Stage 2 qualified bidders must submit a pilot/PoC for their AI engine; detailed PoC scoring/acceptance is not defined in this PQ.

answers.answerText: Prices are prohibited in Stage 1 technical PQ. Financial strength is assessed via solvency evidence rather than project pricing.

answers.exactQuestionText: What qualification evidence must be authenticated by previous clients or external authorities?
answers.answerText: Completion certificates/client reference letters, official good-performance certificates, bank-issued financial solvency certificate, and security certificates/audit reports are required as evidence.

answers.exactQuestionText: For AI/agentic-chatbot projects, what user-facing channels must be supported now and which are future/optional?
answers.answerText: Web, SANAD mobile app, WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger are target channels; future voice integration is anticipated and Arabic ASR/TTS voice interaction is explicitly optional.

answers.exactQuestionText: What languages, dialects, localization and speech capabilities must the AI support?
answers.answerText: Arabic-first, full Arabic and English, with customization for Jordanian Arabic dialects. Optional Arabic ASR/TTS is included for future voice/accessibility use cases.

answers.exactQuestionText: What AI architecture is required: LLM, RAG, NLU/NLP, agentic/tool use, intent/dialogue management, vector database, model customization, and hallucination controls?
answers.answerText: LLM + RAG + NLU/NLP are required; contextual understanding, intent recognition and dialogue management are explicit. Qualification requires experience with vector databases and strict knowledge to prevent hallucinations. Detailed agent/tool orchestration and model strategy are TBC.

answers.exactQuestionText: What knowledge sources, APIs, repositories and authoritative-data boundaries will ground responses?
answers.answerText: SANAD portals, NSR database, government APIs and knowledge repositories are named. Detailed source ownership, ingestion governance, freshness, approval and source-priority rules are not defined in this PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: What transaction classes may the chatbot execute, and what identity, authentication, payment, document and authorization controls apply?
answers.answerText: Selected e-government services may be executed end-to-end. SANAD APIs support authentication, payments and document retrieval. Exact transaction catalogue and authorization rules are TBC.

answers.exactQuestionText: What live-agent handover, CRM/call-center integration, escalation, sentiment and human-oversight behavior is required?
answers.answerText: Live-agent handover must integrate with existing CRM/call-center systems such as Genesys/Zendesk; sentiment analysis and escalation triggers are required. Detailed human-approval/escalation policies are TBC.

answers.exactQuestionText: What model-quality and safety metrics must be measured: factual accuracy, groundedness, hallucination rate, task success, Arabic dialect quality, toxicity, refusal, latency and user satisfaction?
answers.answerText: The PQ requires accurate/context-aware responses and strict knowledge to prevent hallucinations, but does not define quantitative acceptance thresholds. These should be explicitly defined in Stage 2.

answers.exactQuestionText: What AI evaluation/red-team/test datasets, gold answers, adversarial scenarios and PoC acceptance criteria are required?
answers.answerText: A Stage 2 AI-engine PoC is mandatory, but datasets, metrics, thresholds, red-team scenarios and pass/fail criteria are not specified in this PQ.

answers.exactQuestionText: What model lifecycle, retraining/fine-tuning, prompt/RAG updates, monitoring, drift, versioning and continuous-improvement process is required?
answers.answerText: Maintenance and continuous improvement plus bidder-managed GPU infrastructure for training/optimization are required at high level. Detailed MLOps/model-governance lifecycle is TBC.

answers.exactQuestionText: What AI infrastructure split applies to training, optimization and inference, and how are open/non-open data separated?
answers.answerText: Hybrid environment: MoDEE on-premises plus bidder-provided GPU clusters; on-premises hosting is stated for non-open data and bidder GPU infrastructure for training/optimization of open data. Production inference placement and data-classification rules require clarification.

answers.exactQuestionText: What data residency, privacy, encryption, identity/access and security framework requirements specifically constrain the AI solution?
answers.answerText: All data stored in Jordan; MoDEE cybersecurity/privacy requirements; AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.3 in transit; zero-trust RBAC; ISO 27001/NIST or equivalent evidence.

answers.exactQuestionText: What accessibility and inclusive-conversation requirements apply across text and voice channels?
answers.answerText: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance and an inclusive, accessible, user-centric experience are required. Voice interaction via Arabic ASR/TTS is optional but positioned for accessibility/inclusivity.

answers.exactQuestionText: What analytics, conversation telemetry, sentiment, service-usage and operational dashboards are required?
answers.answerText: Dashboards must cover conversation analytics, service usage and performance metrics; sentiment analysis and feedback/escalation triggers are required. Exact KPIs are TBC.

answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the PQ does not define AI/model/IP/licensing ownership rules.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: SSC has 35 in-scope business processes delivered through walk-in and e-mode channels. The engagement must study both backend processes and related customer-facing/front-end steps, document the current state on the Governmental BPM Platform (ARIS), and prepare redesigned future-state processes.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not predefine a fixed list of current pain points. Instead, the bidder must discover them by analyzing each current process for weaknesses/strengths, stakeholder complexity, unnecessary documents/data requirements, form/checklist inefficiencies, legal/regulatory constraints, and performance gaps measured through KPIs.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: The project is intended to improve SSC service performance and customer satisfaction across walk-in and electronic channels, streamline procedures, enable digital-service delivery, and align future processes with broader government digital-transformation capabilities and shared e-government services.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Document and understand the current SSC process architecture; establish measurable As-Is KPIs; identify weaknesses and complexity; redesign To-Be processes; improve forms/checklists and regulations; support e-mode delivery through government shared services; define stakeholder responsibilities; and produce a gap/execution plan for moving from As-Is to To-Be.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: The project must use the existing Governmental BPM Platform (ARIS), MODEE filter and ARIS Convention Manual, existing process catalogues, current laws/regulations/forms, and current SSC procedures. The To-Be design must also consider existing e-government shared services such as GSB, SGN, Digital Signature, Cloud, Smart Card, SMS Gateway and the National Call Center. No previous contract/phase is explicitly identified.

answers.answerText: The RFP does not define named formal phases, but the required work implies a sequence: mobilization/project planning and training → data gathering → As-Is documentation and KPI baseline → analysis of weaknesses/stakeholders/documents/regulations → To-Be redesign → stakeholder/KPI/form/legal recommendations → gap analysis and execution plan → approvals → project closeout.

answers.answerText: Primary internal stakeholders are SSC employees, process owners and service-delivery teams involved in the 35 processes. answers.answerText: Minimum bidder staffing includes 1 PMP-certified Project Manager and at least 4 full-time on-ground BPR specialists: 2 senior BPR experts and 2 junior BPR experts. All staff must be fluent in Arabic. The work also requires an accredited ARIS trainer and EFQM training arranged through the King Abdullah II Center for Excellence.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?

answers.answerText: The RFP itself and its annexes/mandatory response artefacts govern the procurement, including the Sample Arabic Agreement, Key RFP Dates, Confidentiality Undertaking, Bidder Information, World Bank Anti-Corruption acceptance, mandatory compliance matrix, and the prescribed technical/financial proposal formats.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: MoDEE currently operates a legacy on-premise Data Warehouse and batch-oriented data environment. The new platform must consolidate data from roughly 45 governmental entities and replace the legacy warehouse with a modern open-architecture Lakehouse supporting batch, incremental CDC, real-time streaming, open storage formats, governance and scalable analytics.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: The RFP identifies modernization needs including legacy on-premise warehouse limitations, long/full-extract refresh patterns, proprietary-format lock-in and vertical scalability limits, insufficient real-time/near-real-time integration, log-file/storage inefficiencies, fragmented metadata/governance, data-quality issues, and the need for stronger lineage, security, observability and resilience.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: MoDEE wants to modernize government data infrastructure as part of Jordan's digital-transformation agenda, improve timeliness and governance of data shared across governmental entities, and establish a scalable platform for analytics, BI and future AI/ML use cases while preserving data sovereignty.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Replace the legacy Data Warehouse with a modern open Data Lakehouse; reduce data-refresh cycles; establish centralized metadata, governance, lineage and discoverability; enable wide data sharing/interoperability; support advanced analytics/BI and future AI/ML workloads; decouple storage and compute for scalability; improve resilience; and ensure full data sovereignty in the Government Private Cloud.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: Yes. The solution replaces the existing legacy on-premise Data Warehouse/SQL Server staging environment and must integrate with governmental source systems such as Oracle, SQL Server, REST APIs, SFTP and flat files. Existing MoDEE Active Directory, security monitoring and Government Private Cloud services must also be considered.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there phases? If yes, list them.
answers.answerText: The RFP is organized by implementation workstreams rather than a formal named phase model: architecture/design → infrastructure/platform delivery → data ingestion and CDC → Lakehouse storage → batch/stream processing and orchestration → semantic/query/reporting/analytics → platform administration, training and handover → Preliminary Acceptance → 12-month support/maintenance → Final Acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the expected duration?
answers.answerText: Full implementation within 365 calendar days from commencement, followed by 12 months of support and maintenance from Preliminary Acceptance. Final Acceptance occurs after the maintenance period.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is the beneficiary / system owner?
answers.answerText: MoDEE is the contracting entity, platform owner and primary beneficiary. Data originates from and serves numerous governmental entities; MoDEE technical teams will administer and operate the platform after knowledge transfer.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who are internal users? External users?
answers.answerText: Internal users include MoDEE platform administrators, data engineers, analysts/BI consumers and authorized technical staff. Downstream consumers include BI dashboards, analytics applications, authorized government applications and future AI/ML workloads. At least 12 MoDEE staff must receive in-person training. Exact broader user counts are not specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: What roles are required?
answers.answerText: Minimum bidder staff include 1 Project Manager, 1 Data Lakehouse Architecture Engineer, 2 Data Engineers, and 1 DevOps resource. Support also requires an account/contact person, local support resources and a resident engineer for 3 months. MoDEE may approve or request replacement of key personnel.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?
answers.answerText: Classic business UAT is not explicitly defined. MoDEE provides formal Preliminary Acceptance after all implementation scope is delivered and Final Acceptance after the maintenance period. The RFP requires multiple live demonstrations, validation evidence, benchmarking and compliance proof for core platform capabilities.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who owns the system after go-live?
answers.answerText: MoDEE owns the resulting project artefacts. The RFP states that source code, licenses, documentation, hardware and software procured/developed under NUR V2 Lakehouse become MoDEE property, and contract documents/software remain MoDEE property.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is in scope?
answers.answerText: End-to-end delivery of an on-premise Data Lakehouse and governance platform: target architecture, GPC infrastructure design/provisioning/configuration, batch ingestion, CDC, real-time streaming, open object storage/table formats, batch/stream processing, orchestration, semantic/query layer, data catalog/governance/lineage, security, HA/DR, observability, secrets management, IaC/CI-CD, performance benchmarking, documentation, training/shadowing, handover and 12 months of support.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is out of scope?
answers.answerText: Explicit exclusions/constraints include: API management is outside scope; no public-cloud dependency, data transit or storage is permitted; remote implementation is not permitted; the product must not be custom in-house development; and core platform storage must not rely on proprietary closed formats. Other exclusions are not consolidated into a single section.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are bidder responsibilities?
answers.answerText: The winning bidder is responsible for project management, architecture, installation/configuration/integration of all platform components, compute/storage sizing, GPC deployment, security hardening, HA/DR, ingestion/CDC/streaming, processing/orchestration, governance/catalog/lineage, semantic/query layer, observability, IaC/CI-CD/version control, testing/benchmarking, documentation, training, engineer shadowing, handover and post-implementation support.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are MODEE / entity responsibilities?
answers.answerText: MoDEE provides/governs the Government Private Cloud environment and existing enterprise context such as Active Directory, security monitoring and source-system access; reviews/accepts the solution; provides staff for training/shadowing; and controls approvals such as technology substitutions and final acceptance. Detailed environment capacities/data access are to be coordinated during implementation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Assumptions, dependencies, constraints?
answers.answerText: Key constraints/dependencies include 365-day implementation, on-site-only implementation at MoDEE, full on-premise GPC deployment, no public-cloud dependency, fixed lump-sum pricing, supported open-source technologies, no unapproved tool substitutions, data from 45 governmental entities, security/MSB/PDP compliance, existing source-system capabilities/licensing for CDC, and required live demonstrations/benchmarks.

answers.exactQuestionText: Main modules / services?
answers.answerText: Major platform service layers are: batch ingestion; incremental CDC; real-time event streaming; open Lakehouse storage; open table format/catalog; batch and streaming processing; pipeline orchestration; semantic/query layer; data access services; data governance/catalog/lineage; identity/security; observability; HA/DR; and platform administration.

answers.exactQuestionText: Key workflows / approvals?
answers.answerText: The main workflows are data-centric rather than business-transaction workflows: batch ingestion, CDC capture, streaming, schema validation, data-quality checks, transformation, promotion across Land/Structure/Consume zones, orchestration/dependencies/retries, compaction, semantic-layer refresh, governed query access, metadata/cataloging, auditing, deployment/version-control and operational change/rollback workflows.

answers.exactQuestionText: Reports / dashboards / notifications needed?
answers.answerText: Required reporting/monitoring includes observability dashboards, infrastructure/health/capacity dashboards, SLA/SLO monitoring, data-quality reports, benchmark reports, audit logs, lineage visualization, searchable catalog/business glossary, alerting/incident notifications, support/service reports and operational status evidence.

answers.exactQuestionText: Document management / case / ticketing needs?

The platform also requires catalog, metadata and operational documentation repositories.

answers.exactQuestionText: Any AI or advanced features required/optional?
answers.answerText: The platform must support future AI/ML workloads as governed data consumers, but this RFP does not require delivery of AI/ML models or AI functionality as part of the implementation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Hosting / infrastructure model?
answers.answerText: All platform components must be deployed fully on-premise within the Government Private Cloud (GPC). No data may transit or reside on public-cloud infrastructure and no platform component may have public-cloud dependency. The bidder designs, provisions/configures and maintains the required VMs, nodes and software within the GPC environment.

answers.exactQuestionText: Integrations / APIs?
answers.answerText: Integration/data-source requirements include Oracle, SQL Server, REST APIs, SFTP, CSV/XML/JSON and other approved sources; MoDEE Active Directory; existing security monitoring/SIEM; GPC backup services; and downstream BI/analytics/government applications through SQL, JDBC, ODBC and REST where required. API management itself is explicitly outside scope.

answers.exactQuestionText: Security / data residency requirements?
answers.answerText: Security/data-sovereignty requirements are extensive: no data outside government infrastructure; encryption in transit/at rest; TLS 1.2+ and TLS 1.3 for CDC where specified; MFA, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, AD integration, PII discovery/classification, masking, DLP, immutable/tamper-resistant logs, secrets/key management, network segmentation/Zero Trust, centralized audit/security monitoring, MoDEE MSB compliance, and Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 (2023).

answers.exactQuestionText: Performance / availability / backup / DR?
answers.answerText: The solution requires cluster HA, failover, backup/recovery, replication, protected/immutable backups, DR testing, documented component-level RPO/RTO targets, rolling upgrade/rollback capability and operation during node failures. Performance requirements include documented source-to-query latency, sub-second data availability for real-time use cases where stated, sub-second representative query performance, scalable batch/stream processing and performance benchmarking.

answers.exactQuestionText: Data migration needs?
answers.answerText: The RFP requires replacement/migration of the legacy warehouse and supports large historical bulk loads from existing source systems, along with conversion into open columnar/open table formats. It requires handling source schemas, historical snapshots, CDC positions, data quality, schema drift and staged movement through Land/Structure/Consume zones. A separate classical migration plan is not explicitly named.

answers.exactQuestionText: Accessibility requirements? (English drafting only in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: No user-interface accessibility requirement is stated. This is primarily a backend data-platform procurement. Accessibility is therefore not applicable unless introduced for separate user-facing tools outside the current scope.

answers.exactQuestionText: What documents/reports/designs/tests/training materials are required?
answers.answerText: Deliverables include: fully implemented Data Lakehouse; architecture and infrastructure design/as-built documents; component/version matrix; sizing document; licenses; IaC repository; observability and secrets-management configuration; network/security/hardening documentation; CDC/ingestion pipelines and validation reports; storage/catalog configurations; data-quality/schema-governance artefacts; batch/stream/orchestration platforms and CI/CD; benchmark/SLO reports; semantic/query/data-access and IAM configurations; data catalog and lineage; training/shadowing materials; operational runbooks/handover; compliance matrix; and support/service reports.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required formats?
answers.answerText: All final deliverables must be submitted as official documents properly bound, stamped and signed by the winning bidder. The RFP also requires version-controlled repositories for IaC, workflows/configuration/source artefacts, and formal operational/technical documentation. Specific office-file formats for implementation deliverables are not comprehensively stated.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves each deliverable?
answers.answerText: MoDEE is the approving/accepting authority. Preliminary Acceptance is issued after all scope is completed and delivered, before maintenance; Final Acceptance follows completion of the maintenance period. Individual deliverables are subject to validation, demonstrations, compliance evidence and MoDEE review, but the RFP does not map a named approver to every deliverable.

answers.exactQuestionText: Stages, timeline, milestones?
answers.answerText: Overall implementation must be completed within 365 calendar days from commencement. The RFP does not provide a detailed milestone calendar; the implementation is structured across architecture, infrastructure, ingestion/CDC, storage, processing/orchestration, semantic/query/governance, administration/training and acceptance. Twelve months of support follow Preliminary Acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Testing / UAT rounds?
answers.answerText: Testing/validation includes mandatory compliance evidence, live demonstrations of CDC, streaming, multi-step orchestration/failure-retry behavior, Iceberg time-travel/schema evolution/ACID behavior, query-acceleration security, lineage, and performance benchmarking. HA/DR recovery testing and security validation are also required. A traditional end-user UAT cycle is not explicitly defined.

answers.exactQuestionText: Acceptance criteria and go-live conditions?
answers.answerText: Preliminary Acceptance occurs after the bidder finishes and delivers all work in the scope; the 12-month maintenance period starts after Preliminary Acceptance. Final Acceptance occurs after all contract work and the maintenance period are completed. Acceptance is supported by required demonstrations, benchmark/validation reports, compliance matrix and operational handover.

answers.exactQuestionText: Rollback plan needed?
answers.answerText: Yes. The RFP requires rolling-upgrade rollback mechanisms, job/workflow versioning and rollback, metadata/table rollback capability, change-controlled deployment, and rollback plans for pre-planned maintenance that may affect availability or stability.

answers.exactQuestionText: Support period and hours?
answers.answerText: Support and maintenance is required for 12 months after Preliminary Acceptance. Severity 1 and 2 support is 24x7; Severity 3 and 4 support is 08:00-17:00 on working days (Sunday-Thursday). A resident engineer is required for the first 3 months after Preliminary Acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Severity levels / response / resolution times?
answers.answerText: Severity 1: response 1 hour, resolution 8 hours. Severity 2: response 2 hours, resolution 24 hours. Severity 3: response 4 hours, resolution 3 working days. Severity 4: response 8 hours, resolution 5 working days.

answers.exactQuestionText: Resident engineer / ticketing / reports?
answers.answerText: The bidder must provide a contact/account manager, local support team, on-site support when needed, a resident engineer for 3 months, incident communication channels, a ticketing/issue-tracking system accessible to the entity and capable of integration with MoDEE ticketing if requested, escalation procedures, and service/incident reports.

answers.exactQuestionText: Penalties?
answers.answerText: Yes. Severity 1: 10 JD per hour after resolution time for the first 24 hours, then 240 JD/day until resolved. Severity 2: 170 JD/day after resolution time. Severity 3: 130 JD/day; after 4 days MoDEE may call a third party and charge the costs in addition to penalties. Severity 4: 100 JD/day after resolution time. MoDEE may also charge its repair costs and deduct them from dues/bonds.

answers.exactQuestionText: Technical vs financial weights?
answers.answerText: No percentage technical-versus-financial weighting is stated. The overall proposal is evaluated technically and financially and awarded according to Clause 29 of the Government Procurement Instructions of 2022, based on the required compliance sheet.

answers.exactQuestionText: Minimum score / PoC scoring / disqualification rules?
answers.answerText: No minimum technical score or PoC score is stated. Key responsiveness/disqualification conditions include failure to submit the mandatory compliance sheet, failure to meet bidder qualification/certification/reference requirements, missing/incorrect bidder information, non-compliant proposal format, missing bid security, alternative proposals, prohibited tender-document reservations, and other legal/administrative non-compliance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Pricing model and cost breakdown requirements?
answers.answerText: The contract is an all-inclusive fixed lump-sum price in Jordanian Dinars, with implementation, support/maintenance and other costs broken out. Bidders must also provide unit rates in the Bill of Quantities/remuneration schedule and clearly identify costs of all Section 3 activities. Required licenses must be explicitly itemized and included in the total lump sum.

answers.exactQuestionText: Optional priced items? Taxes?
answers.answerText: The 12-month support period is mandatory, not optional. Required licenses are itemized but included in the lump sum. The bidder must commit support prices for one additional year after Final Acceptance. Prices include applicable fees and taxes, including sales tax. No broad optional-scope list is defined.

answers.exactQuestionText: Applicable laws / confidentiality / IP?
