answers.answerText: Applicable requirements include Jordanian laws/regulations, Governmental Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and Instructions, the binding Sample Arabic Agreement, confidentiality/NDA terms, intellectual-property and document-ownership provisions, MoDEE secrecy/security requirements, Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 (2023), and the World Bank Anti-Corruption Guidelines and Sanctions Framework.

answers.exactQuestionText: Joint venture / subcontracting rules?
answers.answerText: Subcontracting is allowed where skills are unavailable, subject to MoDEE approval, and the prime bidder remains liable for subcontracted work. Bidder information must disclose subcontractors/JV members where applicable. Detailed JV governance terms are not otherwise defined in this RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required forms, compliance sheets, questionnaires, annexes?
answers.answerText: Required/controlling artefacts include the mandatory Solution Compliance Matrix; technical and financial response formats; Bill of Quantities/remuneration schedule; Form of Bid and summary payment schedule in the Sample Arabic Agreement; Bid Security; Sample Arabic Agreement; Key RFP Dates; Confidentiality Undertaking; Bidder Information template; and Letter of Acceptance of the World Bank Anti-Corruption Guidelines/Sanctions Framework.

answers.exactQuestionText: What must not be missed in this RFP?
answers.answerText: Critical items not to miss include: replacement of the legacy warehouse; open-source/open-format architecture; all-on-premise GPC/no public cloud; data from ~45 entities; prescribed platform tool classes; mandatory compliance sheet/live demonstrations; full data governance/lineage/PII/security requirements; HA/DR and performance benchmarking; 365-day on-site implementation; fixed lump-sum pricing; qualified local partner/staff; in-person training for at least 12 MoDEE staff; resident engineer/support SLA; and Preliminary/Final Acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mistakes happened in previous similar RFPs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the RFP does not document mistakes from previous similar RFPs.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which parts usually cause vendor questions or scope disputes?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not provide a historical vendor-dispute log, but several clarification-sensitive or internally inconsistent points exist: the deadline is blank; the solution is described for 45 entities while a scalability clause refers to 30+; qualified-bidder references mention one similar project while the technical proposal asks for two similar support/maintenance projects; and the tender-bond clause shows 5,000 JD numerically while also spelling out 'one thousand Jordanian Dinars'. The support text also contains inherited wording such as 'MOIN/NUR system'.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which requirements are mandatory, optional, excluded, or pending approval?
answers.answerText: Mandatory requirements include the compliance matrix, prescribed platform capabilities/tool classes, GPC-only deployment, security/governance, integration, demonstrations/benchmarks, 365-day implementation, training, bidder qualifications and 12-month support. Explicitly excluded/prohibited items include public-cloud dependency, API management, remote implementation and unapproved custom/in-house or closed-format core approaches. Pending/TBC items include the final deadline and bidder-defined sizing/RTO/RPO/benchmark details.

answers.exactQuestionText: What should be priced separately as optional?
answers.answerText: No optional project modules are explicitly separated. Required licenses must be itemized but included in the lump sum; the bidder also commits support prices for one year after Final Acceptance. Any other project-delivery costs are expected to be included rather than treated as unplanned optional extras.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is still unknown and should be [To be confirmed]?
answers.answerText: Key TBCs include the final proposal deadline/key dates; exact source-system volumes and historical data sizes; final compute/storage sizing; exact RPO/RTO targets; some performance/SLO values to be proposed and validated; detailed GPC resource allocations; source-system CDC licensing dependencies; the final support-price schedule after Final Acceptance; and resolution of the noted qualification/bond/entity-count inconsistencies.

answers.exactQuestionText: Should Rami generate a risk/ambiguity list before final drafting?
answers.answerText: The source RFP does not explicitly ask for a pre-drafting risk/ambiguity list. However, it contains several placeholders and inconsistencies that such a quality-control step would detect. For source-grounded answering, treat the requirement itself as [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: What standards, policies, or annexes must be referenced?
answers.answerText: Relevant standards/policies include Government Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and Instructions; Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 (2023); MoDEE Minimum Security Baseline and security/integration policies; Zero Trust principles; TLS/encryption requirements; Active Directory/RBAC/ABAC/MFA/DLP controls; World Bank Anti-Corruption Guidelines/Sanctions Framework; and the mandatory RFP annexes/compliance matrix.

answers.exactQuestionText: What bidder qualification, local-partner/OEM/technology-partner certifications, reference projects, and accomplishment evidence are mandatory?
answers.answerText: Local partner certificate required; at least one similar reference in the last 5 years is stated in qualification, while another section asks for two similar support/maintenance references; accomplishment letters and staff CVs are mandatory.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mandatory proposal response structure, compliance matrix, bidder-information disclosure, and attachments control responsiveness?
answers.answerText: Mandatory compliance matrix, prescribed technical/financial proposal formats, bidder-information template, Bill of Quantities, Form of Bid, payment schedule, Bid Security and other annexes control responsiveness; non-compliance may disqualify the bidder.

answers.exactQuestionText: What proposal security and performance bond are required, and for how long must they remain valid?
answers.answerText: Tender bond/proposal security is stated as 5,000 JD (despite inconsistent wording in the same clause) and must remain valid 90 days after closing or 30 days beyond an agreed extension. Performance bond is 10% of contract value within 14 days of award notification.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the proposal validity period, and what modification/withdrawal rules apply?
answers.answerText: Proposal validity is 90 days. Modification/withdrawal is allowed before the deadline; withdrawal during validity may forfeit proposal security.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the clarification process, contact channel, and key dates?
answers.answerText: Questions go to eGov_tenders@modee.gov.jo with subject 'NUR V2. Lakehouse' and answers are shared on JONEPS. The actual question/answer/deadline dates are blank and must be confirmed.

answers.exactQuestionText: How must technical proposal, financial proposal, and bid bond be submitted?
answers.answerText: Technical/corporate and financial proposals are submitted on JONEPS. The bid bond is a separate hard-copy envelope to the MoDEE tender department. Final deadline is blank/TBC.

answers.exactQuestionText: What anti-corruption, debarment, donor, or sanctions-framework declarations are mandatory?
answers.answerText: A signed Letter of Acceptance of the World Bank Anti-Corruption Guidelines and Sanctions Framework is required and incorporated into the contract for the winning bidder.

answers.exactQuestionText: What subcontracting/JV disclosures and approval requirements apply?
answers.answerText: Subcontracting may be used where skills are unavailable but requires MoDEE approval; the prime bidder remains liable. Bidder information must disclose subcontractors, JV members, local partners and owners.

answers.exactQuestionText: For data-platform/lakehouse projects, what current data estate is being replaced or integrated, including source systems, formats, refresh model, entity count, and current pain points?
answers.answerText: Legacy on-premise Data Warehouse/SQL Server staging is being replaced. Sources include Oracle, SQL Server, REST APIs, SFTP and files. About 45 governmental entities are targeted. The current full-extract/batch model is to be replaced by CDC and real-time/near-real-time ingestion.

answers.exactQuestionText: What ingestion modes and freshness/latency requirements apply: batch, incremental CDC, real-time streaming, historical bulk load, schema drift, and error handling?
answers.answerText: All are required: batch ingestion, log-based CDC, event streaming, historical bulk loads, schema normalization/drift handling, dead-letter queues, data-quality validation and documented source-to-query latency; sub-second data availability is required for real-time use cases.

answers.exactQuestionText: What open-format, storage, table-format, zoning, metadata/catalog, lifecycle, and anti-lock-in requirements apply?
answers.answerText: Open columnar storage with Apache Iceberg (or equivalent), MinIO (or equivalent), Land/Structure/Consume zones, ACID, schema evolution, time-travel, metadata catalog/versioning, lifecycle/retention/legal hold, and no proprietary closed core storage formats.

answers.exactQuestionText: What data governance, catalog, lineage, quality, PII, masking, RBAC/ABAC, auditing, and data-protection requirements apply?
answers.answerText: Native governance/metadata/lineage, searchable catalog/business glossary, PII discovery/classification, masking, DLP, RBAC/ABAC, AD integration, immutable auditing and Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 (2023) compliance are mandatory.

answers.exactQuestionText: What processing, orchestration, workflow-versioning, CI/CD, data-quality, SLO, retry, and rollback capabilities are required?
answers.answerText: Spark batch/stream processing, Kafka streaming, Airflow code-defined workflows, version control, CI/CD, data-quality framework, SLA/SLO monitoring, retry/back-off, dependency management, job versioning and rollback are required.

answers.exactQuestionText: What semantic/query-layer, BI/data-access, federation, query-acceleration, security, and performance targets apply?
answers.answerText: A governed semantic/query layer such as Dremio is required, with SQL/JDBC/ODBC/REST access, federated access, query acceleration, RBAC/RLS/column masking and representative sub-second query-performance validation.

answers.exactQuestionText: What infrastructure sizing, growth, HA/DR, backup, RPO/RTO, observability, secrets, network-security, and upgrade requirements apply?
answers.answerText: Bidder sizes compute/storage for ~45 entities and security/backup/DR overhead; must provide HA/DR and RPO/RTO, backup/replication, observability/logging/tracing, secrets management, segmentation/Zero Trust, IaC and rolling upgrade/rollback procedures.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mandatory technology/tool constraints exist, and what substitutions/equivalents require approval or proof?
answers.answerText: Required tool classes include NiFi, Debezium, Kafka + Spark Structured Streaming, Spark, Airflow, MinIO, Iceberg, Dremio and native governance capabilities (or equivalents). Substitution requires prior written MoDEE approval; supported versions and production-deployment evidence are required.

answers.exactQuestionText: What live demonstrations, proof points, benchmark scenarios, and acceptance evidence must bidders provide?
answers.answerText: Live or documented demonstrations are required for CDC, streaming, Airflow failure/retry, Iceberg time-travel/schema evolution/ACID, query acceleration/security, lineage and end-to-end workflows; benchmark reports and operational SLOs are also required.

answers.exactQuestionText: What knowledge-transfer, shadowing, operational-handover, documentation, and post-implementation-independence outcomes are required?
answers.answerText: In-person training for at least 12 MoDEE staff, training environment/materials/assessment, Engineer Shadowing Program, comprehensive runbooks/admin/security/backup/governance documentation, handover and a support model intended to make MoDEE independently capable are required.

answers.exactQuestionText:
What type of RFP/document is this?
(system implementation / framework agreeme...
answers.answerText: System implementation / mixed engagement: implementation of an Integrated Tax Administration Solution (ITAS), including design, development, customization, integration, data migration, training, organizational change, cloud deployment, and long-term operations & maintenance.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the document/RFP title?
answers.answerText: Request for Proposal (RFP) Document for Implementation of Integrated Tax Administration Solution for Income sale and Tax Directorate — Volume 2B: Integrated Tax Administration Solution - Terms of Reference.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the beneficiary entity / ministry?
answers.answerText: Primary beneficiary/system owner: Income & Sales Tax Department (ISTD). The RFP is issued by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE), with ISTD as the operating tax authority.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the RFP or tender number (if any)?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the cover shows the placeholder RFP No. "XXXXX" rather than a finalized tender number.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the deadline?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the cover shows the placeholder deadline "00/00/2025" rather than a finalized submission deadline.

answers.exactQuestionText: Language is English only for now (do not ask for Arabic/bilingual in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: The RFP volume itself is in English, but the project is bilingual. Business-facing services and communications must support Arabic and English; deliverables such as BRDs are required in Arabic and English, while some technical deliverables such as HLD/LLD may be in English.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which approved template or reference RFP should be followed?
answers.answerText: No previous reference RFP/template is named in this volume. The governing references are this Volume 2B Terms of Reference and ITAS Annexures A-N, including Functional Requirements, Technical Requirements, Interfacing Systems, Data Points, Technology Stack, IDM, Government Service Bus, Government Web Standards, Customer Journey Standards, Performance Test Checklist and e-service Performance KPIs.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: ISTD is modernizing tax administration after legislative, audit, control and electronic-linking reforms. It currently operates existing e-services and a Core Tax System and must support a very large taxpayer base and many internal users. The current environment requires modernization, integration, data migration and improved digital service delivery.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: Key problems/needs stated in the RFP include improving tax justice and audit efficiency; combating tax evasion and avoidance; improving performance and efficiency of the revenue system; improving taxpayer service quality; reducing manual/paper-based tax processing; modernizing legacy systems; integrating fragmented information sources; and improving operational transparency, accessibility and taxpayer experience.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: The project is part of the Government of Jordan's economic and tax-administration reform agenda. Following legislative, audit and electronic-linking reforms, ISTD decided to implement ITAS as a strategic initiative to modernize tax administration, improve services and strengthen revenue-system efficiency without relying on higher tax rates.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Implement a modern, integrated, tax-agnostic administration platform that improves taxpayer self-service and service quality, strengthens audit/compliance/enforcement, reduces manual work, provides integrated taxpayer information and analytics, improves efficiency and transparency, supports additional taxes in the future, and enables secure multi-channel digital services.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: Yes. The bidder must consider the existing e-services/Core Tax System, legacy data and documents, current integrations with government and third-party systems, existing service channels and call center, and MoDEE's existing Government Private Cloud (GPC) arrangement. Migration and transition from the legacy environment are core project dependencies.

answers.exactQuestionText:
Is this a one-time project, framework agreement, system implementation,
consu...
answers.answerText: A large-scale system implementation and digital-transformation engagement covering software implementation, customization, integrations, data migration, cloud deployment, training, organizational change, project governance, and a 10-year operations & maintenance/support period after preliminary acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there phases? If yes, list them.
answers.answerText: Yes. The implementation lifecycle includes project inception; requirements gathering and gap analysis; BRD/SRS and detailed design/configuration; development/customization and testing in phased releases; iterative and consolidated UAT; environment readiness; beta, performance and security testing; production deployment; data migration; go-live/stabilization; training and change management; then long-term O&M/support.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the expected duration?
answers.answerText: Implementation is intended to be completed within 2 years. Operations and Maintenance then continues for 10 years after Preliminary Acceptance, with possible further extension at ISTD's discretion.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is the beneficiary / system owner?
answers.answerText: ISTD is the principal beneficiary and operational owner of ITAS. MoDEE is a key project authority/governance stakeholder and provides the Government Private Cloud environment. Project deliverables and source code become property of MoDEE/ISTD.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who are internal users? External users?
answers.answerText: Internal users include ISTD tax officers, staff, administrators, call-center/helpdesk users and other internal operational users. External users include taxpayers (individuals, employees, companies and partnerships), tax agents, legal representatives, government departments/agencies, banks and Tax Service Providers. The RFP states 1,600 ISTD user logins and 1,419 active ISTD users, plus a registered taxpayer population of about 1.826 million.

answers.exactQuestionText: What roles are required?
answers.answerText: System roles include taxpayers, tax agents, legal representatives, ISTD tax officers/staff/admins, government-agency users and service providers. The bidder must also provide a substantial project team including project/program management, tax/domain experts, solution/integration/database/security architects, infrastructure/network experts, testing, BI/analytics, UI/UX, training, quality, operations and change-management specialists, with defined experience/certification requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?
answers.answerText: ISTD and MoDEE provide formal sign-offs throughout the lifecycle. ISTD signs off gap analysis, BRD/SRS, prototypes, design/configuration and other deliverables. UAT is performed with ISTD/MoDEE/business owners and relevant third parties, with iterative UAT for releases plus a final consolidated UAT. Go-live requires ISTD/MoDEE acceptance and Preliminary Acceptance certification.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who owns the system after go-live?
answers.answerText: MoDEE/ISTD owns the ITAS project documents and source code. The winning bidder operates and maintains the system for 10 years after Preliminary Acceptance, but ownership of the system artefacts/source code remains with MoDEE/ISTD.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is in scope?
answers.answerText: Supply and implementation of ITAS application modules; installation of associated peripherals/accessories; requirements, design, development and customization; web portal/mobile/services; CRM, workflow/case/document/content management; integrations/APIs; BI/reporting; security; GPC cloud deployment; data conversion/cleansing/migration; testing and UAT; training/knowledge transfer; organizational change management; PMO/governance; on-site resources; helpdesk; application enhancement/maintenance; and 10 years of O&M.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is out of scope?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not provide one complete out-of-scope list. Explicit responsibility exclusions/limits include: underlying GPC infrastructure is provided/managed by MoDEE; operating-system licenses and underlying infrastructure are provided by MoDEE/ISTD; and the winning bidder is not responsible for procuring/supplying/maintaining the call-center IT/non-IT infrastructure. Other exclusions should be confirmed.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are bidder responsibilities?
answers.answerText: The winning bidder is responsible for end-to-end ITAS solution delivery: requirements/gap analysis, architecture/design, licenses and solution components, development/customization, integrations/APIs, data migration, testing, deployment, documentation/source code, training, OCM, project management, staffing, GPC application-layer deployment/configuration, helpdesk L2/L3, SLA monitoring, maintenance/enhancement, issue/change/release management, security compliance and O&M.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are MODEE / entity responsibilities?
answers.answerText: ISTD/MoDEE provide business input, reviews and sign-offs; participate in workshops and UAT; provide/coordinate GPC hosting and underlying infrastructure services; provide relevant data, legacy-system access and stakeholder coordination; manage L1 call-center support; provide workspace/tools for designated in-house resources; and govern approvals, security/compliance and acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Assumptions, dependencies, constraints?
answers.answerText: Key constraints/dependencies include a 2-year implementation target; 10-year O&M; 10% annual growth to be considered for sizing; GPC hosting; extensive legacy/external integrations; migration from e-services/Core Tax System; Arabic communication/localization requirements; evolving detailed requirements during BRD/SRS; 24/7 availability; government security/web standards; multiple testing/UAT rounds; and on-site/offshore staffing constraints.

answers.exactQuestionText: Main modules / services?
answers.answerText: Main ITAS functional areas include Taxpayer e-Services; Registration; Returns & Declarations; Payments; Compliance & Audit; Enforcement; Legal/Appeals/Courts; Information & Deductions/Exemptions; Customer Relationship Management; Refunds; Dashboard & Reporting; BI & Analytics; plus document/content management, workflow/case management, business rules, web portal, mobile app and API-driven external interfacing.

answers.exactQuestionText: Key workflows / approvals?
answers.answerText: The system must support end-to-end tax-administration workflows for registrations, returns/declarations, payments, refunds, compliance/audits, enforcement/debt collection, exemptions, legal cases/appeals, taxpayer inquiries and service requests. Workflow/case management includes activity assignment, approvals, escalations, business rules, audit trails and role-based processing. Detailed workflows and approval matrices are finalized during BRD/SRS.

answers.exactQuestionText: Reports / dashboards / notifications needed?
answers.answerText: Required reporting includes a 360-degree taxpayer view, MIS, dashboards, BI/analytics, management reports, KPI/KRA visualizations, compliance/audit/debt/payment statistics, real-time SLA monitoring dashboard, alerts/reminders/notifications/correspondence, audit trails and periodic O&M/SLA/project-status reports.

answers.exactQuestionText: Document management / case / ticketing needs?
answers.answerText: Yes. ITAS requires enterprise content/document management, workflow management, case management, CRM/service-request management, audit trails and electronic records retention. Operational support also requires helpdesk/CRM routing and bug/issue tracking for L1/L2/L3 support and resolution.

answers.exactQuestionText: Any AI or advanced features required/optional?
answers.answerText: No explicit Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning requirement is stated in this Volume 2B. Advanced capabilities do include BI/analytics, data warehousing, risk engines, rules engines, 360-degree taxpayer analytics and automated monitoring/alerts.

answers.exactQuestionText: Hosting / infrastructure model?
answers.answerText: ITAS will be hosted on the Government Private Cloud (GPC), provided and managed by MoDEE. GPC provides services such as VMs, load balancer, WAF, DNS/publishing, object storage, backup, warm DR, antivirus, SSL, SMTP and SMS integration. The winning bidder deploys/configures the ITAS application layer and is responsible for solution-specific software/licenses and cloud application configuration.

answers.exactQuestionText: Integrations / APIs?
answers.answerText: ITAS is API-driven and must integrate with internal and external stakeholder systems using APIs and potentially a Government Service Bus/API-management layer. Integrations include IDM/SSO/SANAD, payment services such as eFAWATEERcom and banks, CRM/call center, multiple government agencies/ministries, Tax Service Providers and other present/future tax or third-party systems. Annexure C contains interfacing systems.

answers.exactQuestionText: Security / data residency requirements?
answers.answerText: Security requirements include Zero Trust and Defense-in-Depth/layered security; WS-Security across infrastructure, applications, web services, integration points and channels; IDM/SSO and MFA; security logging/auditing; vulnerability/penetration testing; data integrity, masking and access control; and compliance with MoDEE/ISTD security requirements. Hosting is on the Government Private Cloud and operations are Jordan-based, but a separate explicit data-residency clause is not stated in this volume.

answers.exactQuestionText: Performance / availability / backup / DR?
answers.answerText: ITAS must support 24/7 availability, high performance and minimal downtime, redundancy, replication, load balancing, scalability, hot-standby/high availability, backup and disaster recovery, RPO/RTO objectives, warm DR, capacity planning and peak-load sizing. Annexure L defines e-service performance KPI thresholds. Sizing must factor 10% annual growth over the 10-year maintenance horizon.

answers.exactQuestionText: Data migration needs?
answers.answerText: Extensive data migration is required from the current e-services/Core Tax System and physical/digital sources. Scope includes extraction, conversion, cleansing, mapping, metadata tagging, digitization, archival, mock migrations, reconciliation, testing, governance/versioning, cutover planning and production migration, with migration design/execution/cutover plans and formal ISTD sign-off.

answers.exactQuestionText: Accessibility requirements? (English drafting only in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: Yes. ITAS must comply with Jordan Government Websites Standards and related checklists/customer-journey standards for usability and universal accessibility. Front-end/back-end channels must be responsive across devices/browsers, and the system must support Arabic and English.

answers.exactQuestionText: What documents/reports/designs/tests/training materials are required?
answers.answerText: Required deliverables include project charter/plan; gap analysis; BRD, SRS and RTM; process maps/personas/journey maps/prototypes; architecture and configuration documents; HLD/LLD/database/deployment design; integration/API documentation; dashboard/analytics reports; source code and deployment scripts; data-migration plans/reports; quality plans and test plans/cases/reports; SIT/UAT/security/performance results; user/system/admin manuals; training materials; OCM/change plans; go-live/stabilization reports; helpdesk setup; SLA/O&M reports; policies/SOPs; and ongoing change/issue/status reports.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required formats?
answers.answerText: The RFP requires standardized documentation and signed-off deliverables. Business deliverables such as BRDs must be in Arabic and English; some technical deliverables such as HLD/LLD may be in English. Training materials and government-stakeholder training are bilingual. Exact office-file formats are not comprehensively prescribed in this volume.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves each deliverable?
answers.answerText: ISTD and/or MoDEE approve/sign off deliverables. The schedule explicitly requires ISTD sign-off for gap analysis, BRD/SRS, prototypes, system design/configuration, migration, deployment, manuals and go-live; MoDEE/ISTD sign off dashboard/analytics and content; business owners participate in UAT and sign UAT certificates. ISTD has 15 working days to approve/reject/provide feedback on submitted deliverables.

answers.exactQuestionText: Stages, timeline, milestones?
answers.answerText: The implementation schedule starts at Contract Award (T). Key milestones include project charter/key staff at T+2 weeks; gap analysis T+6; BRD T+20; SRS/dashboard work T+24; design/configuration T+28; development/testing up to T+68; UAT support and environment readiness T+88; beta/performance/security testing T+96; production deployment and production data migration T+103; go-live/stabilization and helpdesk go-live T+104. O&M then continues for 10 years.

answers.exactQuestionText: Testing / UAT rounds?
answers.answerText: Testing includes unit/sprint testing, system/integration testing, SIT/end-to-end, multiple UAT preparations for up to 3 releases plus a final consolidated UAT, security testing, load/performance testing, beta testing and MODEE's own functional/non-functional testing rounds. The winning bidder must resolve defects and support ISTD during UAT.

answers.exactQuestionText: Acceptance criteria and go-live conditions?
answers.answerText: Go-live/preliminary acceptance requires a detailed Go-Live Plan, completed data migration, SIT/integration testing, performance/load and security testing, UAT assistance/sign-off, required environments, completed training, beta-test clearance, deployment and migration sign-offs, approved manuals/designs/source code, security/load/unit/system acceptance reports, and a Go-Live Certificate from ISTD. O&M begins after final Preliminary Acceptance.

answers.exactQuestionText: Rollback plan needed?
answers.answerText: Yes. Change-management requirements state that all change plans must be backed by rollback plans. Data migration also requires cutover planning and transition controls.

answers.exactQuestionText: Support period and hours?
answers.answerText: Continuous support is required during phased rollout and throughout a 10-year Operations & Maintenance period after Preliminary Acceptance. ITAS must operate 24/7, with planned maintenance during off-business hours/weekends/ISTD holidays. The bidder provides L2/L3 application support and dedicated helpdesk resources; L1 is handled by ISTD call-center agents.

answers.exactQuestionText: Severity levels / response / resolution times?
answers.answerText: The SLA defines Severity 1, 2 and 3 incidents. Severity 1 incidents must be resolved within 60 minutes; Severity 2 within 4 hours; Severity 3 within one working day. Additional SLA measures include reopened incidents, availability/performance and other operational parameters, with automated SLA monitoring.

answers.exactQuestionText: Resident engineer / ticketing / reports?
answers.answerText: The bidder must establish a technical helpdesk with dedicated manpower for L2/L3 support, integrated with the ISTD call-center CRM; ISTD call-center agents provide L1. All issues are logged/tracked, monthly issue logs are submitted, escalation paths are required, and many key project resources must be onsite during defined phases.

answers.exactQuestionText: Penalties?
answers.answerText: Yes. Liquidated damages apply for SLA breaches. Implementation-phase SLA damages are capped at 10% of contract value; repeated SLA failures can double damages; sustained operations penalties may lead to termination and forfeiture of the Performance Bank Guarantee. Failure to reach Go-Live within 6 months of the planned date due to the bidder can trigger termination for default.

answers.exactQuestionText: Technical vs financial weights?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — this Volume 2B Terms of Reference does not state the overall technical-versus-financial evaluation weighting. Bidder resources/CVs are noted as subject to technical evaluation, but the scoring model appears to belong to other RFP volumes.

answers.exactQuestionText: Minimum score / PoC scoring / disqualification rules?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — this Volume 2B does not provide the overall minimum technical score, PoC scoring or full bid-disqualification rules. It does state mandatory compliance with the ToR, standards, staffing and acceptance requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Pricing model and cost breakdown requirements?
answers.answerText: The scope repeatedly requires costs for required activities/tools to be included in the bidder's fixed lump sum price. The bidder must price solution licenses/components and provide financials for training options in Fin-Form 4.6. The full financial breakdown/payment schedule is not fully presented in this Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: Optional priced items? Taxes?
answers.answerText: Optional/separately priced items explicitly mentioned include certain OS/database licenses not provided by GPC and two training options (Training-the-Trainer for ~15% of the team vs training all ~1350+ personnel). The document also lists estimated costs for additional testing rounds, but indicates extra rounds beyond official testing may be borne by the winning bidder. Tax treatment is not specified in this Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: Applicable laws / confidentiality / IP?
answers.answerText: This Volume 2B does not comprehensively state governing law/confidentiality clauses. It does require strong MoDEE/ISTD security compliance and states that all ITAS documents and source code become property of MoDEE/ISTD. Security, access-control, audit and data-protection obligations are extensive. Broader legal/contractual terms should be confirmed from the other RFP volumes.

answers.exactQuestionText: Joint venture / subcontracting rules?
answers.answerText: The document defines bidders/participants as shortlisted firms responding either as a single bidder or as a consortium with multiple participants, but detailed joint-venture/subcontracting rules are not set out in this Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required forms, compliance sheets, questionnaires, annexes?
answers.answerText: The Volume includes/references ITAS Annexures A-N: Functional Requirements; Technical Requirements; ISTD Interfacing Systems; Data Points; Technology Stack; IDM; Government Service Bus; Government Web Standard; Government Web Standard Checklist; MODEE Customer Journey Standards Compliance Report 2020; Performance Test Checklist; e-service Performance KPIs; ITS Program Plan; and Additional Requirements. Compliance sheets/templates are also required during BRD/SRS and proposal response.

answers.exactQuestionText: What must not be missed in this RFP?
answers.answerText: Critical items not to miss include: 2-year implementation and 10-year O&M; existing-system/data migration; GPC hosting responsibility split; 10% annual sizing growth; API-driven integrations; Arabic/English support; 24/7 availability; security/Zero Trust; full testing/UAT and acceptance regime; extensive manpower/on-site requirements; training and OCM; PMO/governance; SLA monitoring and liquidated damages; source-code/document ownership; and the detailed Annexures A-N.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mistakes happened in previous similar RFPs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — this Volume does not document mistakes from previous similar RFPs.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which parts usually cause vendor questions or scope disputes?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not document historical vendor questions or disputes. However, it explicitly leaves several items to later requirements gathering/finalization, including final user lists, detailed services/processes, interfaces, data volumes, some O&M onsite requirements and evolving BRD/SRS details; these are likely clarification-sensitive areas but no historical dispute record is provided.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which requirements are mandatory, optional, excluded, or pending approval?
answers.answerText: Mandatory requirements include the functional/technical scope, GPC deployment, integrations, security, migration, testing/UAT, bilingual requirements, manpower, training, PMO, SLA and O&M obligations. Optional/separately priced areas include some licenses and training options. Pending/finalized-later items include detailed business requirements, final personas/users, certain integrations/data volumes, some resource deployment details and requirements refined during BRD/SRS.

answers.exactQuestionText: What should be priced separately as optional?
answers.answerText: Items explicitly suitable for separate/optional pricing include bidder-responsible OS/database licenses not provided by GPC and the two training options in Fin-Form 4.6. Other optional commercial items should be confirmed from the financial volume.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is still unknown and should be [To be confirmed]?
answers.answerText: Key TBCs include the final RFP number and deadline; detailed future-state business requirements; final user/persona list; exact interfaces/API specifications; final data volumes/migration detail; detailed technology/BOM choices; some resource deployment requirements during O&M; requirements that will be refined in BRD/SRS; and the full financial/evaluation/legal terms contained outside Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: Should Rami generate a risk/ambiguity list before final drafting?
answers.answerText: The RFP requires formal risk and issue management, quality risk evaluations, change control and PMO governance, but it does not explicitly request a pre-drafting 'risk/ambiguity list' in the way Rami's question asks. Treat that decision as [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: What standards, policies, or annexes must be referenced?
answers.answerText: Key references include PMI standards/best practices; Agile methodology; ITSM standards; ISO 27001 certification/testing; Jordan Government Websites Standards and checklist; MODEE Customer Journey Standards; GPC Policy; MoDEE/ISTD security guidelines; WS-Security; Zero Trust/Defense in Depth; OEM/technology-owner certification standards; and ITAS Annexures A-N.

answers.exactQuestionText: How many bidders/suppliers will be awarded, and what is the award model?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — award model/number of winners is not stated in Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: If this is a framework agreement, how will work orders/call-offs be issued, allocated, rotated, or reopened during the framework period?
answers.answerText: Not applicable to this system-implementation ToR as written. If the wider procurement uses framework/call-off mechanics, they are outside Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: What minimum bidder/company eligibility and previous-experience requirements apply?
answers.answerText: Volume 2B focuses on solution/manpower requirements. Detailed corporate eligibility/track-record rules should be confirmed from the procurement/evaluation volume.

answers.exactQuestionText: What minimum staffing qualifications, experience levels, and resource quantities are mandatory?
answers.answerText: Extensive requirements are defined: two dedicated in-house resources (Tax Expert and Project Manager), plus a key-resource matrix covering program/project management, architecture, infrastructure, testing, tax/domain, BI, security, training, quality, UI/UX, integration and change management with experience/certification expectations.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the clarification process and clarification deadlines?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — not stated in Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: How must proposals be submitted? (physical/electronic, address/portal, copies, envelopes/files, technical/financial separation)
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — proposal submission mechanics are not stated in Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the proposal validity period, and what are the modification/withdrawal rules?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — not stated in Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are bid bonds, performance bonds, guarantees, or other securities required? If yes, when and at what value?
answers.answerText: A Performance Bank Guarantee is referenced as subject to forfeiture for serious SLA failure, but its required amount/timing is not specified in Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: Is a PoC, demonstration, pilot, presentation, or other pre-award qualification exercise required? What is its process and timing?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no pre-award PoC/demo process is specified in Volume 2B. The implementation does require prototypes, demos, beta testing and iterative UAT after award.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there specific bidder response templates, compliance sheets, declarations, or mandatory attachments that control proposal acceptance?
answers.answerText: Yes. The bidder is expected to update requirement-compliance columns in Annexures, provide staffing/CV information and detailed technical/project plans; however the complete proposal-response package is outside Volume 2B.

answers.exactQuestionText: What baseline transaction/user/data volumes, growth assumptions, peak loads, and sizing horizon must the solution support?
answers.answerText: The RFP gives key taxpayer/user counts and requires 10% annual growth to be factored into application/infrastructure sizing for the 10-year maintenance period. Detailed data points are referenced in Annexure D.

answers.exactQuestionText: What language, localization, translation, and bilingual deliverable requirements apply to the system, communications, content, training, and project documents?
answers.answerText: ITAS must support Arabic and English across user channels. BRDs and many business deliverables must be bilingual; some technical documents may be English. Communication is expected in Arabic, with translation for foreign experts the bidder's responsibility; training includes Arabic/English delivery.

answers.exactQuestionText: What architecture principles, technology-stack constraints, integration patterns, identity standards, and mandatory design standards must the solution follow?
answers.answerText: The solution is API-driven, may use GSB/API management and SOA, integrates with IDM/SSO/MFA, follows Zero Trust/Defense in Depth, and must align to ITAS Technical Requirements, Technology Stack, Government Service Bus and other annexures.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the exact responsibility split for hosting, infrastructure, licenses, backup/DR, network connectivity, and application-layer cloud deployment?
answers.answerText: MoDEE/GPC provides and manages underlying Government Private Cloud services and core infrastructure; the winning bidder deploys/configures the ITAS application layer, supplies solution-specific software/licenses and manages application-level requirements, capacity and compliance.

answers.exactQuestionText: What training, certification, knowledge-transfer, and handover obligations apply, for which user groups and in what quantities?
answers.answerText: The bidder must provide initial and ongoing training/knowledge transfer, training-needs analysis, role-based curricula, Arabic on-site training, OEM-aligned certification tracks, and price two options covering ~1350+ personnel including a Train-the-Trainer option.

answers.exactQuestionText: What Organizational Change Management (OCM), adoption, stakeholder communication, and business-readiness requirements apply?
answers.answerText: The RFP requires an OCM strategy and approach integrated into the program, plus stakeholder communication/change plans, training and go-live readiness activities.

answers.exactQuestionText: What PMO, governance, reporting, risk/issue management, change control, escalation, and decision-making model is required?
answers.answerText: The winning bidder must establish a PMO aligned with PMI best practices, provide a detailed project plan/governance model, hold weekly/monthly meetings, manage risks/issues/change control/SLA/transition, maintain minutes and reporting, and provide escalation mechanisms.

answers.exactQuestionText: What manpower model applies across phases, including on-site/offshore requirements, mandatory roles, experience, certifications, replacement rules, and deployment schedules?
answers.answerText: A detailed key-resource matrix and staffing/deployment plan are mandatory. Key resources work onsite during defined phases, development may occur offshore, two dedicated in-house resources are stationed with MoDEE for the 2-year contract, and replacement/onsite compliance rules apply.

answers.exactQuestionText: What operational support model is required after go-live (L1/L2/L3, helpdesk, ITSM processes, support staffing, incident/problem/change/release management)?
answers.answerText: L1 is handled by ISTD call-center agents; L2/L3 by the winning bidder's dedicated helpdesk, integrated through CRM. O&M requires ITSM processes, issue/problem/bug tracking, change/version/release management, SLA monitoring and full-time support resources.

answers.exactQuestionText: What ownership, source-code, documentation, transition/exit, portability, and post-contract handover requirements apply?
answers.answerText: All ITAS documents and source code become property of MoDEE/ISTD. The project charter requires an exit-management plan, documentation must remain updated, and transition/exit management is a formal governance activity.

answers.exactQuestionText:
What type of RFP/document is this?
(system implementation / framework agreeme...
answers.answerText: Connectivity/telecom Open Framework Agreement for managed and unmanaged internet/connectivity services, including MPLS, 5G, Satellite Internet, All-Type/Private VPN, 4G SIM and other connectivity services.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the document/RFP title?
answers.answerText: Open Framework Agreement Request for Proposal for Internet and Connectivity Services.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the beneficiary entity / ministry?
answers.answerText: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MODEE), Jordan, serving participating government entities across the Kingdom.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the RFP or tender number (if any)?
What is the deadline?
answers.answerText: 19 November 2025 at 3:00 PM, Amman local time.

answers.exactQuestionText: Language is English only for now (do not ask for Arabic/bilingual in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: The RFP is primarily in English, with some Arabic contractual/tax text and an Arabic Sample Contract Agreement referenced as binding.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which approved template or reference RFP should be followed?
answers.answerText: The RFP itself, the MODEE standard components/compliance sheet, the Technical and Financial Proposal Response Formats, Key RFP Dates and Deadlines, RFP Terminology, and the binding Sample Arabic Agreement govern the response and contract.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: MODEE needs a unified framework to procure and manage connectivity for government entities across Jordan using multiple technologies. Government sites require reliable access to online platforms, applications, inter-agency communication and remote services, with consistent service management and support.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not describe a specific failed legacy project, but it addresses risks/needs around service continuity, uneven coverage, outages, network resilience, redundancy, secure access, scalability, performance, standardized procurement, monitoring and support across government locations.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: The project supports the Government of Jordan's ongoing digital-transformation effort by strengthening national government connectivity, operational continuity and access to digital services, while standardizing connectivity procurement through a centralized MODEE-managed framework.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Provide reliable, high-speed and secure connectivity; improve resilience and redundancy; support scalable digital-transformation services across regions; enable secure VPN access; standardize procurement and management; and ensure uninterrupted government operations through defined SLA, monitoring and support requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: No previous framework/contract is identified. The services must interoperate with existing government networks and systems, and VPN/private VPN is expected to work over MPLS, 4G/5G, fiber, satellite and other broadband. Exact existing site connectivity and HQ connectivity are not fully defined.

answers.exactQuestionText:
Is this a one-time project, framework agreement, system implementation,
consu...
answers.answerText: A five-year Open Framework Agreement for recurring connectivity services. It combines telecom service procurement, site-by-site activation, operations, maintenance, monitoring, support and mini-tender/direct-order purchasing mechanisms.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there phases? If yes, list them.
answers.answerText: There is no single software-style phase plan. The lifecycle is demand-driven: framework qualification/award → site coverage confirmation → service allocation or MPLS mini-tender/direct PO → installation/activation → 10-day testing → ongoing 24/7 operation/support → changes, upgrades, transfers or cancellation as requested.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the expected duration?
answers.answerText: Five years for the Open Framework Agreement. Individual MPLS contract duration is to be determined and agreed by MODEE.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is the beneficiary / system owner?
answers.answerText: MODEE is the framework owner and central procurement/governance entity. Participating government entities are the operational beneficiaries of the connectivity services.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who are internal users? External users?
answers.answerText: This is not an application-user project. Operational users/stakeholders include MODEE/e-Government Operations Center teams, government-entity IT teams and users/employees consuming internet, VPN and government systems. Exact user counts are not specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: What roles are required?
answers.answerText: The provider must assign a dedicated project manager, technical focal point and 24/7 liaison/contact; provide technical installation teams; operate a 24/7 NOC and helpdesk; support on-site/remote fault resolution; and provide escalation contacts. MODEE and government IT teams coordinate requests and approvals.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?
answers.answerText: There is no formal UAT. MODEE authorizes service requests and changes, the provider verifies activation on site, and each new connection has a 10-day testing period before official activation. Planned outages require approval from the concerned government entity.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who owns the system after go-live?
answers.answerText: Not applicable as a software system implementation. However, the RFP states that source code, licenses, documentation, hardware and software procured or developed under the framework become MODEE property upon conclusion, and contract documents/software remain MODEE property.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is in scope?
answers.answerText: Provision, design, installation, configuration, testing, activation, operation, monitoring, maintenance and support of MPLS, 5G, Satellite Internet, All-Type/Private VPN, 4G SIM and other requested connectivity. Scope includes CPE/hardware, civil works where needed, redundancy, security, NOC/helpdesk, monitoring tools, incident/change management, reporting, site transfers, upgrades and project coordination.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is out of scope?
answers.answerText: No comprehensive out-of-scope list is stated. Explicit limits include: a bidder is not obligated to provide a service where coverage is unavailable; satellite customers provide mounting location and power; and actual subscriptions are activated only when required. Other exclusions should be confirmed.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are bidder responsibilities?
answers.answerText: The bidder is responsible for end-to-end service delivery and operation: network design, coverage confirmation, all required equipment and installation, configuration, site activation, testing, monitoring, NOC/helpdesk, security, incident/change management, reporting, maintenance, replacement of faulty equipment, escalation, project management, technical support and compliance with SLA/regulations.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are MODEE / entity responsibilities?
answers.answerText: MODEE coordinates with government entities, shares site lists/coordinates, issues formal service requests/POs, authorizes installation/disconnection/transfer/speed changes, manages fair allocation under the framework, determines approved pricing, and coordinates/approves planned outages. Government entities provide site readiness/power where stated.

answers.exactQuestionText: Assumptions, dependencies, constraints?
answers.answerText: Key dependencies/constraints include actual site coverage, site readiness, provider technology coverage, official PO/service request, nationwide/regional availability, five-year framework rules, no guaranteed minimum subscription quantity, defined activation times, 10-day testing, fixed/unified pricing, cybersecurity/TRC compliance and service-specific SLA requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Main modules / services?
answers.answerText: Service catalogue: Managed MPLS L2/L3; Unmanaged MPLS L2/L3; Unmanaged MPLS L2 Q-in-Q; 5G Internet; Satellite Internet; All-Type/Private VPN (including IPSec/SSL/Remote Access concepts); 4G SIM; and any other connectivity service MODEE may require during the framework.

answers.exactQuestionText: Key workflows / approvals?
answers.answerText: Key operational workflow: MODEE identifies a site/need → providers confirm coverage/service type → MODEE allocates the service fairly or runs an MPLS mini-tender/direct purchase → provider installs and activates → 10-day test → official operation/billing → monitoring/support → formal MODEE authorization for upgrades/transfers/disconnections → incident escalation and reporting as needed.

answers.exactQuestionText: Reports / dashboards / notifications needed?
answers.answerText: Required monitoring/reporting includes a web-based real-time monitoring tool, link utilization/performance/fault monitoring, monthly SLA compliance reports, periodic uptime/latency/incident reports, monthly usage reports, incident root-cause/corrective-action reports, and a MODEE dashboard for tracking line-management activities.

answers.exactQuestionText: Document management / case / ticketing needs?
answers.answerText: Yes, operational support must include helpdesk, ticketing system and hotline channels, incident management/escalation, service-request communication channels, and tracking/reporting of issues. The RFP does not require a separate enterprise document/case-management platform.

answers.exactQuestionText: Any AI or advanced features required/optional?
answers.answerText: No AI or AI-enabled feature is requested.

answers.exactQuestionText: Hosting / infrastructure model?
answers.answerText: This is a telecom infrastructure/service model rather than an application-hosting model. Providers operate their own network backbone/NOC and supply CPE, routers/modems, gateways, cables, software and required installation/civil works. MPLS should use high-redundancy backbone design; access may use fiber, microwave or other media where necessary.

answers.exactQuestionText: Integrations / APIs?
answers.answerText: No API integration requirements are specified. Network interoperability is required: VPN/Private VPN must integrate with MPLS, 5G, fiber, satellite and other broadband; 5G may integrate with VPN/MPLS/hybrid networks. Other system/application integration detail is not defined.

answers.exactQuestionText: Security / data residency requirements?
answers.answerText: Services must comply with MODEE cybersecurity policies and TRC requirements. Requirements include physical/logical isolation, VPN routing separation, controlled access, encrypted VPN tunnels, secure connectivity and data privacy/integrity. No explicit data-residency requirement is stated.

answers.exactQuestionText: Performance / availability / backup / DR?
answers.answerText: Connectivity must be 24/7. MPLS specifies minimum 99% availability and redundant dual-path/no-single-point-of-failure design; satellite specifies 99% or vendor SLA and latency ≤200 ms. Severity 1 response/resolution are 1 hour/5 hours, Severity 2 are 2 hours/24 hours. 5G/VPN are best-effort/shared with SLA-based latency/TTR. Backup/DR is not a relevant requirement here.

answers.exactQuestionText: Data migration needs?
answers.answerText: No data migration is required. Service relocation and migration between connectivity types are supported: site-to-site transfer must be completed within 7 days, and MODEE may migrate from one service type to another and terminate the old subscription without penalty except consumed service charges.

answers.exactQuestionText: Accessibility requirements? (English drafting only in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: No accessibility requirement is stated; this is a connectivity-service procurement rather than a public-facing application/UI project.

answers.exactQuestionText: What documents/reports/designs/tests/training materials are required?
answers.answerText: Deliverables include network design diagrams, installed CPE/equipment, NOC and monitoring access, routing policies, SLA/performance reports, escalation matrix, project plan, periodic progress reports, monthly usage reports, incident/root-cause reports, coverage information, dedicated support/focal-point contacts and line-management dashboard capability.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required formats?
answers.answerText: Operational deliverable file formats are generally not specified. Proposal submission must include one hard copy and one soft copy on flash memory in Microsoft Office 2010 or compatible formats; monthly invoices use a standardized MODEE template.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves each deliverable?
answers.answerText: MODEE governs/accepts services and formal changes; the concerned government entity participates in site readiness and outage approval. Each new connection is tested for 10 days before official activation, and MODEE may disconnect without charge during that period if quality is unsatisfactory.

answers.exactQuestionText: Stages, timeline, milestones?
answers.answerText: There is no single project-wide implementation milestone plan because activations are demand-driven. Service activation timelines are defined by service and number of links: MPLS 1-10 within 7 business days, 11-50 within 15, 51-100 within 20, above 100 by agreed plan; 5G/4G 1-20 within 3 days, 21-100 within 7, above 100 by agreed plan; satellite groups of 10 sites within 15 business days subject to readiness/coverage. Site transfer is within 7 days.

answers.exactQuestionText: Testing / UAT rounds?
answers.answerText: Each new connection requires a 10-day service-quality testing period before official activation. No software-style SIT/UAT rounds are required.

answers.exactQuestionText: Acceptance criteria and go-live conditions?
answers.answerText: Acceptance is operational: the provider must verify service is fully activated before leaving the site, the connection undergoes a 10-day quality test, and no charges apply if MODEE disconnects during the test due to unsatisfactory quality. Ongoing service must meet technical/SLA requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Rollback plan needed?
answers.answerText: No formal rollback plan is specified. Controlled changes require formal MODEE authorization, and service-type migration/cancellation rules are defined.

answers.exactQuestionText: Support period and hours?
answers.answerText: 24/7 technical support, 365 days a year, throughout the five-year framework for active services. Providers must operate 24/7 NOC/helpdesk support with monitoring, troubleshooting and on-site/remote support.

answers.exactQuestionText: Severity levels / response / resolution times?
answers.answerText: Severity 1 (complete outage): response within 1 hour and resolution within 5 hours. Severity 2 (service degradation): response within 2 hours and resolution within 24 hours. Other service-specific TTR/MTTR parameters refer back to the SLA.

answers.exactQuestionText: Resident engineer / ticketing / reports?
answers.answerText: Required: 24/7 NOC and helpdesk, customer-support ticketing/hotline, dedicated project manager/technical focal point, 24/7 liaison officer, escalation matrix, periodic performance reports, monthly SLA/usage reports and incident/root-cause reports. No resident engineer is explicitly required.

answers.exactQuestionText: Penalties?
answers.answerText: Yes. Response delay: 2 JD per incident per line until acknowledgment/action. Resolution delay: 3 JD per hour per incident per line after the allowed resolution time. Late activation: 10% × (PO value / implementation period) per day. Faulty hardware must be replaced within 3 days at no extra cost. External uncontrollable failures may be exempt with official proof.

answers.exactQuestionText: Technical vs financial weights?
answers.answerText: No percentage technical-versus-financial weighting is stated. Award is based on lowest compliant proposals per service/speed under Government Procurement Instructions Article/Clause 29; MPLS is technically evaluated first and later procured through mini-tenders with financial proposals based on specific requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Minimum score / PoC scoring / disqualification rules?
answers.answerText: No minimum technical score or PoC score is stated. Compliance/disqualification rules include late or non-compliant submissions, alternative proposals, missing signed mandatory forms, attempts to influence evaluation, prohibited tender-document reservations, and other responsiveness requirements. MODEE may reject offers and is not bound to select any offer.

answers.exactQuestionText: Pricing model and cost breakdown requirements?
answers.answerText: Bidders provide monthly unit prices by service and speed, except MPLS which is procured via direct order/mini-tender. Billing is based on actual monthly active subscriptions. Prices are in JOD, inclusive of expenses/fees/taxes, with a clear price breakdown. Participating framework prices are fixed/unified, subject to MODEE price-review rules.

answers.exactQuestionText: Optional priced items? Taxes?
answers.answerText: Static IP addresses are priced in the service list. Other connectivity services may be added during the framework. All installation, relocation, cancellation and additional fees are the bidder's responsibility and should not be charged separately to MODEE. Financial offers include applicable taxes, including sales tax (normally 16% unless supported 0% treatment applies).

answers.exactQuestionText: Applicable laws / confidentiality / IP?
answers.answerText: Applicable framework includes the laws/regulations of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, Governmental Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and its Instructions, the binding Sample Arabic Contract Agreement, MODEE secrecy/security requirements, NDA/confidentiality obligations, intellectual-property provisions and MODEE ownership rights over contract material/documents/software as specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Joint venture / subcontracting rules?
answers.answerText: Sub-contractors are contemplated and the winning bidder remains fully responsible for services performed by them; confidentiality, conflict-of-interest and IP obligations extend to sub-contractors. Detailed joint-venture rules are not stated in this RFP text.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required forms, compliance sheets, questionnaires, annexes?
answers.answerText: Annexes listed are: 9.1 Technical Proposal Response Format; 9.2 Financial Proposal Response Format; 9.3 RFP Terminology; 9.4 Key RFP Dates and Deadlines; 9.5 Sample Arabic Agreement; 9.6 Compliance Sheet. The Form of Bid attached to the Sample Arabic Agreement must be completed, signed and stamped.

answers.exactQuestionText: What must not be missed in this RFP?
answers.answerText: Critical points include the five-year open framework; partial service-by-service award; all-region coverage; MPLS/5G/Satellite/VPN/4G technical requirements; fair purchasing/allocation mechanism; no minimum subscription commitment; fixed/unified pricing with market-price review; MPLS mini-tenders; service activation timelines; 10-day testing; 24/7 NOC/helpdesk; SLA and penalties; performance and proposal securities; TRC/cybersecurity compliance; and binding Sample Arabic Agreement/compliance sheet.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mistakes happened in previous similar RFPs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the RFP does not document mistakes from previous similar RFPs.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which parts usually cause vendor questions or scope disputes?
answers.answerText: No historical dispute log is provided. Potential clarification-sensitive items explicitly left open include the inquiry email/dates, HQ connectivity, MPLS contract duration, exact site lists/quantities, some MTTR/TTR values stated only 'as per SLA', and the technical details/implementation mechanism of the line-management dashboard.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which requirements are mandatory, optional, excluded, or pending approval?
answers.answerText: Mandatory items include technical/service requirements, coverage confirmation, CPE/equipment, activation/testing, 24/7 support, SLA, reporting, TRC/cybersecurity compliance, proposal/admin/legal requirements and the compliance sheet. Optional/variable items include service types a bidder chooses to offer, static IP and other future connectivity services. Pending items include actual sites/quantities, some MPLS details and later dashboard details.

answers.exactQuestionText: What should be priced separately as optional?
answers.answerText: Static IP is explicitly priced in the service list; additional/future connectivity services may also require pricing. Installation, relocation, cancellation and additional fees should not be priced as extra charges to MODEE because the bidder bears those costs. MPLS pricing is handled through direct orders/mini-tenders rather than the same monthly unit-price mechanism.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is still unknown and should be [To be confirmed]?
answers.answerText: Still TBC: clarification contact email and inquiry/response dates; exact government sites and quantities; HQ connectivity; MPLS individual contract duration; some coverage/media details per site; detailed line-management dashboard technical mechanism; and site-specific requirements that will be defined through requests/mini-tenders.

answers.exactQuestionText: Should Rami generate a risk/ambiguity list before final drafting?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not explicitly ask for a pre-drafting risk/ambiguity list. For Rami, this should remain an internal quality-control action rather than a mandatory content question unless MODEE/BA requests it.

answers.exactQuestionText: What standards, policies, or annexes must be referenced?
answers.answerText: Relevant references include MODEE cybersecurity policies, Telecommunications Regulatory Commission (TRC) requirements, industry best practices, MPLS protocol/QoS requirements, Government Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and Instructions, the binding Sample Arabic Agreement, compliance sheet and MODEE standard components.

answers.exactQuestionText: How many bidders/suppliers may be awarded, and is the award full, partial, multi-supplier, or service-specific?
answers.answerText: Partial, service-by-service award. Each service may be awarded to one or more companies based on compliant price and coverage; MPLS follows a technical qualification then mini-tender process.

answers.exactQuestionText: If this is a framework agreement, how are call-offs, work orders, mini-tenders, or subscriptions allocated among participating suppliers?
answers.answerText: MODEE requests updated coverage, then allocates services fairly/balanced among providers with coverage. MPLS is purchased through post-framework mini-tenders/direct orders based on MODEE's specific requirements.

answers.exactQuestionText: Is there a guaranteed minimum quantity/value, or is demand entirely call-off/actual-need based?
answers.answerText: No minimum number of subscriptions is guaranteed. Activation and billing are based on actual needs and actual monthly active subscriptions.

answers.exactQuestionText: Can framework prices be reviewed or re-opened during the agreement? If yes, what mechanism applies?
answers.answerText: Yes. If market prices fall significantly, MODEE may request revised proposals, adopt the lowest revised prices uniformly, and retain only companies accepting the revised price.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the clarification process, contact, and deadlines?
answers.answerText: The process is specified, but the email and inquiry/response dates are placeholders and therefore remain [To be confirmed].

answers.exactQuestionText: How must proposals be submitted, and what technical/financial separation or mandatory format rules apply?
answers.answerText: Submit to MODEE Tender Department by 19/11/2025 3:00 PM, one hard copy and one soft copy in Office 2010-compatible format, in a sealed/wrapped envelope. Financial and technical proposals are described as separate components but are opened in the same session and submitted in one envelope.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the proposal validity period, and what withdrawal/modification rules apply?
answers.answerText: 90 days from closing. Written modification/withdrawal is allowed before the deadline; withdrawal after deadline or during validity can forfeit the 5,000 JD proposal security.

answers.exactQuestionText: What proposal security, performance bond, guarantees, or other securities are required?
answers.answerText: Proposal security is 5,000 JD as referenced in withdrawal rules. Winning bidder(s) must submit a 20,000 JD performance bond within 10 days of award notification.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there mandatory response templates, compliance sheets, forms, or annexes that control responsiveness?
answers.answerText: Yes: Technical Proposal Response Format, Financial Proposal Response Format, Form of Bid in the Sample Arabic Agreement, Compliance Sheet, and other annexes. Missing signed mandatory forms can make the bid non-responsive.

answers.exactQuestionText: What bidder eligibility, regulatory licensing, geographic coverage, or provider-qualification constraints apply?
answers.answerText: The RFP solicits local qualified ISPs; services should be available across North, Central and South regions; bidders must comply with TRC requirements and demonstrate service coverage.

answers.exactQuestionText: For connectivity/telecom projects, what service families and sub-types must be procured, and which are mandatory versus bidder-selectable?
answers.answerText: MPLS managed/unmanaged L2/L3 and Q-in-Q, 5G, Satellite, All-Type/Private VPN, 4G SIM, and future connectivity services. Providers may bid for all or any listed service types.

answers.exactQuestionText: What geographic/site coverage is required, and how will coverage be validated before each order?
answers.answerText: Coverage is required across Jordan's North, Central and South regions. MODEE shares site lists/coordinates and providers submit updated site coverage before allocation/order. A provider is not obliged where coverage is unavailable but may need to provide proof.

answers.exactQuestionText: What service-specific bandwidth, latency, availability, redundancy, QoS/CoS, and performance targets apply?
answers.answerText: Targets differ by service: MPLS includes specified speeds, 99% availability, dual-path/no SPOF and at least 5 CoS levels; satellite requires ≥150 Mbps down, ≥20 Mbps up and ≤200 ms latency; 5G/VPN are best-effort with SLA monitoring; all active services operate 24/7.

answers.exactQuestionText: What CPE, modem/router, gateway, installation, civil-work, power, and equipment-replacement responsibilities apply?
answers.answerText: Provider supplies/installs/maintains required CPE/equipment and generally covers installation/civil works; site power/readiness responsibilities vary by service. Faulty hardware must be replaced on-site, generally free of charge, and SLA notes require replacement within 3 days.

answers.exactQuestionText: What activation, testing, transfer/relocation, upgrade, and cancellation timelines/rules apply?
answers.answerText: Activation timelines vary by service/link count; new connections require a 10-day test; service transfer between sites must be within 7 days; operational changes require formal MODEE authorization; migration between service types can terminate the old service without penalty except consumed charges.

answers.exactQuestionText: What NOC/helpdesk, monitoring, ticketing, reporting, incident, escalation, and dashboard capabilities are required?
answers.answerText: 24/7 NOC/helpdesk, proactive monitoring, ticketing/hotline, dedicated focal point, escalation matrix, monthly SLA/usage reports, incident RCA/corrective-action reports, real-time monitoring and a line-management dashboard are required.

answers.exactQuestionText: What regulatory, cybersecurity, telecom-protocol, network-isolation, and security-control requirements apply?
answers.answerText: MODEE cybersecurity policies and TRC requirements apply. MPLS must support defined protocols/QoS, physical/logical isolation and separated routing; VPN services require encrypted secure tunnels and access controls.

answers.exactQuestionText: What commercial charging unit applies to each service (monthly subscription, bandwidth tier, direct PO, mini-tender, usage, etc.)?
answers.answerText: Most services are priced monthly by service/speed and billed on active subscriptions; MPLS is procured via direct order/mini-tender. Prices are unified/fixed within the framework subject to formal market-price review.

answers.exactQuestionText:
What type of RFP/document is this?
(system implementation / framework agreement / consulting / assessment /
support / connectivity-telecom / other)
answers.answerText: Open Framework Agreement for Performance Assessment services, covering Performance, Load and Stress Testing of MoDEE digital products.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the document/RFP title?
answers.answerText: OPEN FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT FOR PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the beneficiary entity / ministry?
answers.answerText: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE), Jordan.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the RFP or tender number (if any)?
What is the deadline?
answers.answerText: 1 July 2026 at 12:00 PM, Jordan local time.

answers.exactQuestionText: Language is English only for now (do not ask for Arabic/bilingual in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: English.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which approved template or reference RFP should be followed?
answers.answerText: No separate previous RFP is named. The procurement is governed by this RFP and its annexes, especially the Technical Proposal Response Format, Financial Compliance Sheet, Information Security Policies, and the referenced Sample Framework Agreement.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the current situation?
answers.answerText: MoDEE operates and supports digital products including e-services, websites, mobile applications and infrastructure, and requires qualified companies to be available to assess the performance of these digital products.

answers.exactQuestionText: What pain points exist today?
answers.answerText: The RFP does not identify specific existing incidents. The concerns to be addressed are performance bottlenecks, scalability, responsiveness, maximum concurrent-user capacity, stability and resilience of digital services.

answers.exactQuestionText: Why is this project needed now?
answers.answerText: No specific triggering event is stated. The stated need is to ensure secure and stable launch, operation and resilience of MoDEE digital products.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the objectives and expected impact?
answers.answerText: Assess Performance, Load and Stress behavior; identify bottlenecks; determine maximum concurrent users; assess front-end and back-end performance; determine readiness status; identify failure sources; and provide enhancement recommendations.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there previous phases, systems, or contracts to consider?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no previous performance-assessment contract or earlier project phase is identified in the RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText:
Is this a one-time project, framework agreement, system implementation,
consulting service, assessment, support contract, PoC, or mixed?
answers.answerText: A 24-month Open Framework Agreement for professional Performance, Load and Stress Testing services, with qualification through technical evaluation and a PoC followed by work-order-based implementation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there phases? If yes, list them.
answers.answerText: Yes. Phase 1: Technical Qualifications Evaluation (technical proposal, references, staff qualifications, PoC and evaluation). Phase 2: Work Order and Agreement Implementation (MoDEE issues SOW/work orders with project-specific requirements, activities and deliverables).

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the expected duration?
answers.answerText: 24 months.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who is the beneficiary / system owner?
