answers.answerText: Primary contracting entity: MoDEE. Individual government entities/e-service owners may be beneficiaries of specific testing work orders.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who are internal users? External users?
answers.answerText: Not defined as application users because this is a testing-service framework rather than a system implementation. Testing must simulate end-user traffic.

answers.exactQuestionText: What roles are required?
answers.answerText: At minimum: one Project Manager with a bachelor's degree and at least five years of experience managing professional performance-testing projects; two Performance Testers with bachelor's degrees and at least five years of experience in Stress, Load and security tests; and a competent engineer present at the concerned institution during the examination period.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves? Who does UAT?
answers.answerText: There is no traditional UAT. MoDEE evaluates the PoC against its standards. Work-order/test completion is formally signed off by MoDEE or the relevant government entity/e-service owner.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who owns the system after go-live?
answers.answerText: Not applicable as a system implementation. However, project documents, reports, software and other contract materials developed or procured under the engagement become property of MoDEE.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is in scope?
answers.answerText: Performance, Load and Stress Testing of one or more e-service portals, websites and mobile applications. Activities include simulating end-user traffic; hardware/software performance testing; static/dynamic resource testing; determining maximum concurrent users; identifying bottlenecks; Green/Orange/Red readiness evaluation; front-end and back-end performance assessment; required retesting rounds; reporting; and enhancement recommendations.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is out of scope?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the RFP does not define a formal out-of-scope list.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are bidder responsibilities?
answers.answerText: Conduct tests; build scenarios; identify prerequisites; provide required resources/tools; perform required rounds and retests; provide on-site engineering support; submit status and assessment reports; identify failure causes; provide recommendations; and provide sign-off documentation.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are MODEE / entity responsibilities?
answers.answerText: MoDEE selects the PoC digital product, prepares/provides requested environment setup, issues official test execution orders, prepares SOWs for work orders, defines special requirements/activities/deliverables, and signs off work with the relevant government entity where applicable.

answers.exactQuestionText: Assumptions, dependencies, constraints?
answers.answerText: Work is demand/work-order driven. Actual products, special requirements and some deliverables are defined per work order. Testing must start within 18 hours of work-order issuance. Work-order allocation depends on available projects, number of qualified companies, running projects, company performance and resource availability.

answers.exactQuestionText: Main modules / services?
answers.answerText: Performance Testing, Load Testing and Stress Testing, including front-end and back-end assessment.

answers.exactQuestionText: Key workflows / approvals?
answers.answerText: Operational flow: Work Order → Prerequisite Review → Test Execution → Report → Retest(s) if required → Sign-off. PoC flow: MoDEE selects product → bidder provides prerequisites → MoDEE prepares environment → bidder confirms → MoDEE issues execution order → bidder starts within 18 hours → report/evaluation.

answers.exactQuestionText: Reports / dashboards / notifications needed?
answers.answerText: Periodic status reports; Performance/Load/Stress assessment report; statistics and graphs; readiness status; failure/source analysis; and enhancement recommendations. No dashboard or automated notification system is specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Document management / case / ticketing needs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no document-management, case-management or ticketing platform requirement is specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Any AI or advanced features required/optional?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no AI or advanced-feature requirement is specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Hosting / infrastructure model?
answers.answerText: No vendor-hosted solution is being procured. Tests may cover MoDEE e-services, websites, mobile apps and related hardware/software infrastructure.

answers.exactQuestionText: Integrations / APIs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no specific API or integration requirements are listed.

answers.exactQuestionText: Security / data residency requirements?
answers.answerText: The bidder must comply with MoDEE secrecy/security requirements, attached Information Security Policies, Supplier Relationship Management Policy, and confidentiality requirements. Data residency is not explicitly specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Performance / availability / backup / DR?
answers.answerText: Performance is the core subject of the engagement: responsiveness, scalability, concurrent users, bottlenecks and front/back-end metrics must be assessed. No specific backup or disaster-recovery requirement is stated.

answers.exactQuestionText: Data migration needs?
answers.answerText: Not applicable / not specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Accessibility requirements? (English drafting only in Phase 1)
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no accessibility requirement is specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: What documents/reports/designs/tests/training materials are required?
answers.answerText: Front-end Performance, Load and Stress assessment; back-end Performance, Load and Stress assessment; Performance/Load/Stress report with Executive Summary/readiness status, scope, approach/methodology, hardware/software test results, source-of-failure/root-cause information, statistics/graphs, and enhancement recommendations; periodic work-order status reports; signed SLA/work-order completion form; and details of completed activities.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required formats?
answers.answerText: Exact final report file format is not mandated in the scope. Annex 5.4 requires bidders to describe deliverable format and structure and gives MS Word as an example.

answers.exactQuestionText: Who approves each deliverable?
answers.answerText: MoDEE and/or the relevant government entity/e-service owner signs the completion form. PoC deliverables are evaluated by MoDEE.

answers.exactQuestionText: Stages, timeline, milestones?
answers.answerText: Overall framework: 24 months. Operational SLA: testing starts within maximum 18 hours of work-order issuance; prerequisite check maximum 1 working day; Round 1 + report maximum 2 working days; retest Round 2 or later + report maximum 2 working days. PoC report commitment is 1 day in the evaluation criteria.

answers.exactQuestionText: Testing / UAT rounds?
answers.answerText: A PoC is required during qualification. During implementation, as many testing/retesting rounds as required must be performed to ensure system stability.

answers.exactQuestionText: Acceptance criteria and go-live conditions?
answers.answerText: Qualification requires at least 70/100 overall technical score and at least 35/50 in the PoC. Operational completion requires meeting testing/reporting requirements and formal sign-off by MoDEE or the relevant entity. Traditional go-live is not applicable.

answers.exactQuestionText: Rollback plan needed?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — no rollback plan is specified and traditional deployment rollback is not applicable to this testing-service framework.

answers.exactQuestionText: Support period and hours?
answers.answerText: The framework lasts 24 months. This is not a conventional support contract and fixed support hours are not stated. Testing must start within 18 hours of a work order. Delivery periods are calculated on working days Saturday–Thursday.

answers.exactQuestionText: Severity levels / response / resolution times?
answers.answerText: No incident severity model is specified. Instead: start testing within 18 hours; prerequisite review within 1 working day; initial test/report within 2 working days; retest/report within 2 working days.

answers.exactQuestionText: Resident engineer / ticketing / reports?
answers.answerText: A competent engineer must be present at the concerned institution during the examination period. Periodic status reporting is required. No ticketing platform is specified.

answers.exactQuestionText: Penalties?
answers.answerText: MoDEE may enforce penalties for unjustifiable delivery delay according to the Sample Framework Agreement; the penalty value is determined there for each day of delay.

answers.exactQuestionText: Technical vs financial weights?
answers.answerText: No combined technical-versus-financial percentage split is stated. Technical evaluation totals 100 points: Company References and Track Record 20%, Team Resumes and Staff Qualifications 30%, and PoC Performance Test Report 50%. Financial proposals are reviewed for technically qualified bidders and evaluated for compliance with required prices.

answers.exactQuestionText: Minimum score / PoC scoring / disqualification rules?
answers.answerText: Minimum overall technical score: 70/100. Minimum PoC score: 35/50. Disqualification can result from missing required reference projects, missing PoC, missing commitment to provide required CVs, non-compliance with the Financial Compliance Sheet/Section 3, or including price information in the technical proposal.

answers.exactQuestionText: Pricing model and cost breakdown requirements?
answers.answerText: All-inclusive fixed lump sum pricing in Jordanian Dinars, inclusive of all fees and taxes, with a clear breakdown. Annex 5.3 gives per-e-service prices: Performance Test Round 1 JD 250; Load Test Round 1 JD 250; Stress Test Round 1 JD 250; Performance Retest JD 150; Load Retest JD 150; Stress Retest JD 150.

answers.exactQuestionText: Optional priced items? Taxes?
answers.answerText: No optional items are explicitly identified. All prices must include fees and taxes, including sales tax.

answers.exactQuestionText: Applicable laws / confidentiality / IP?
answers.answerText: Laws of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan; Government Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and its Instructions; Sample Framework Agreement; confidentiality/NDA requirements; MoDEE secrecy/security requirements; conflict-of-interest, liability and indemnity provisions; and MoDEE ownership of contract materials/IP produced under the engagement.

answers.exactQuestionText: Joint venture / subcontracting rules?
answers.answerText: Permitted where skills are unavailable, subject to conditions. Subcontractors require MoDEE approval and the prime contractor remains liable. JV partners are jointly and severally liable and must appoint a managing member/leader.

answers.exactQuestionText: Required forms, compliance sheets, questionnaires, annexes?
answers.answerText: Annex 5.1 Confidentiality Undertaking; Annex 5.2 Information Security Policies / Supplier Relationship Management Policy; Annex 5.3 Financial Compliance Sheet; Annex 5.4 Technical Proposal Response Format; Annex 5.5 Joint Venture Agreement is listed in the Table of Contents. The Sample Framework Agreement is also repeatedly referenced as a binding procurement/contract document.

answers.exactQuestionText: What must not be missed in this RFP?
answers.answerText: Required reference projects; PoC; required resource/CV commitment; compliance with Section 3; signed Financial Compliance Sheet; no financial information inside the technical proposal; and meeting the minimum 70/100 technical score and 35/50 PoC score.

answers.exactQuestionText: What mistakes happened in previous similar RFPs?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — not stated in this RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which parts usually cause vendor questions or scope disputes?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — the RFP does not identify historical vendor-question or scope-dispute areas.

answers.exactQuestionText: Which requirements are mandatory, optional, excluded, or pending approval?
answers.answerText: Mandatory requirements are defined across the scope, evaluation criteria, compliance sheet and proposal instructions. No explicit optional scope is listed. Work-order-specific/pending items include the exact e-service/application, individual SOW, special requirements, additional activities/deliverables, PoC digital product, some PoC timing, number of work orders, and performance-bond value/timing.

answers.exactQuestionText: What should be priced separately as optional?
answers.answerText: No optional services are identified. The RFP instead defines separate unit prices for first-round tests and retests.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is still unknown and should be [To be confirmed]?
answers.answerText: Exact future projects/e-services; work-order-specific scope; special requirements; exact number of work orders; exact PoC product; some PoC scheduling; performance-bond value/timing; and explicit out-of-scope items.

answers.exactQuestionText: Should Rami generate a risk/ambiguity list before final drafting?
answers.answerText: [To be confirmed] — this instruction is not stated in the source RFP.

answers.exactQuestionText: What standards, policies, or annexes must be referenced?
answers.answerText: MoDEE standards; International Standards for performance assessment; Government Procurement By-Law No. 8 of 2022 and its Instructions; Sample Framework Agreement; MoDEE Information Security Policies; Supplier Relationship Management Policy; Confidentiality Undertaking; Financial Compliance Sheet; Technical Proposal Response Format; and JV documentation where applicable.

answers.exactQuestionText: How many bidders/suppliers will be awarded, and what is the award model?
answers.answerText: The top 2 companies will be awarded based on the response evaluation. The agreement is an open framework agreement.

answers.exactQuestionText: If this is a framework agreement, how will work orders/call-offs be issued, allocated, rotated, or reopened during the framework period?
answers.answerText: MoDEE prepares the SOW for each intended work order and submits it to a winning bidder. Work orders are distributed among winning companies one after another. Participation in the framework reopens every 3 months for one week after signing with the first bidders. Allocation may consider available projects, number of qualified companies, active projects, company performance and resource availability.

answers.exactQuestionText: What minimum bidder/company eligibility and previous-experience requirements apply?
answers.answerText: Relevant project references are required. The RFP asks for at least 3 related penetration/performance-testing projects in the last 3 years in Phase 1, while the evaluation section scores 2 similar projects in the last 3 years. A business registration certificate is also required.

answers.exactQuestionText: What minimum staffing qualifications, experience levels, and resource quantities are mandatory?
answers.answerText: One Project Manager with at least a bachelor's degree and at least 5 years of project-management experience in professional performance-test projects; two Performance Testers with at least bachelor's degrees and at least 5 years of Stress, Load and security-test experience.

answers.exactQuestionText: What are the clarification process and clarification deadlines?
answers.answerText: RFP inquiries must be sent in writing to eGov_tenders@modee.gov.jo. Inquiries are accepted until 18 June 2026 and responses are to be issued by 24 June 2026, with Q&A shared with bidders' primary contacts.

answers.exactQuestionText: How must proposals be submitted? (physical/electronic, address/portal, copies, envelopes/files, technical/financial separation)
answers.answerText: Submission deadline is 1 July 2026 at 12:00 PM Jordan local time. The technical/corporate capabilities proposal is submitted in a sealed envelope with 1 hard copy and 1 soft copy via VDR. The technical proposal must not contain price/cost information; including price causes disqualification. The original hard copy prevails in case of discrepancy.

answers.exactQuestionText: What is the proposal validity period, and what are the modification/withdrawal rules?
answers.answerText: Proposals remain valid for 90 days from the closing date. Proposals may be modified or withdrawn before the submission deadline through written notice. Withdrawal after the deadline or during the validity period may lead to forfeiture of proposal security.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are bid bonds, performance bonds, guarantees, or other securities required? If yes, when and at what value?
answers.answerText: No bid bond is required in Phase 1. The winning bidder must submit a performance bond; its value and timing are determined separately for each assignment.

answers.exactQuestionText: Is a PoC, demonstration, pilot, presentation, or other pre-award qualification exercise required? What is its process and timing?
answers.answerText: Yes. MoDEE selects a digital product for the PoC and determines the timeframe. The bidder provides prerequisites and dependencies, MoDEE prepares the environment, the bidder confirms it, MoDEE issues the execution order, and the bidder must start within 18 hours. The PoC is worth 50% of technical evaluation and requires at least 35/50 to pass.

answers.exactQuestionText: Are there specific bidder response templates, compliance sheets, declarations, or mandatory attachments that control proposal acceptance?
answers.answerText: Yes. Required/controlling items include the signed Financial Compliance Sheet, Technical Proposal Response Format, references template, required CV commitment, confidentiality undertaking, information-security policies, and JV documentation where applicable.
